name: Airborne
text:
Rulebook: A card bearing this sigil will strike an opponent directly, even if there is a creature opposing it.

Airborne is a sigil that makes the card bearing it able to strike the opponent directly, even if there is a creature opposing it. 

Behaviour:
If a card with this sigil attacks a space occupied by a card with the Mighty Leap sigil, the Airborne creature cannot attack directly on that space and must attack the defending creature instead, though may attack other spaces directly by using Bifurcated Strike or Trifurcated Strike. An Airborne creature is still vulnerable to attacks from non-Airborne creatures.

name: Amorphous
text:
Rulebook: When a card bearing this sigil is drawn, this sigil is replaced with another sigil at random.

Amorphous is a sigil which becomes another sigil at random when the card bearing it is drawn. 

Notes:
- Amorphous will only transform into sigils with the internal tag Part1Modular in Act I and Part3Modular when in Act III. Additionally, it will only transform into sigils that have a Sigil Power of 0-5, meaning that Sigils with negative power such as Annoying or Brittle are excluded.
- In Act I, Amorphous can sometimes turn into Sigils only present in Kaycee's Mod. This is likely because the Sigils are present in the rulebook for Act I, but otherwise do not appear naturally.

name: Annoying
text:
Rulebook: The creature opposing a card bearing this sigil gains 1 Power.

Annoying is a sigil that causes the card in the lane opposing the sigil to gain 1 Power.

Annoying appears in Kaycee's mod in the Annoying Starters challenge, which adds the Annoying sigil to all starting cards not including pelts. This can result in cards having 3 natural sigils present.

name: Ant Spawner
text:
Rulebook: When a card bearing this sigil is played, an Ant is created in your hand.

Ant Spawner is a sigil which creates a Worker Ant in your hand when a card bearing the sigil is played. If a card bearing this sigil is placed onto the board by Corpse Eater, its effect still activates.

name: Armored
text:
Rulebook: The first time a card bearing this sigil would take damage, prevent that damage.

Armored, known as Nano Armor in Act III, is a Sigil that is present in Act III and Kaycee's Mod. It allows a card bearing it to negate the first instance of taking damage. This includes direct damage dealt by opposing attackers, as well as damage from Sigils such as Detonator, Sharp Quills, and Sentry. Armored also prevents the effects of the Touch of Death Sigil from occurring, but cannot block the effects of Steel Trap and Brittle.

name: Attack Conduit
text:
Rulebook: Other creatures within a circuit completed by a card bearing this sigil gain 1 Power.

Attack Conduit is a sigil that causes all cards inside a circuit completed by a card bearing this sigil to gain 1 Power.

name: Battery Bearer
text:
Rulebook: When a card bearing this sigil is played, it provides an Energy Cell to its owner.

Battery Bearer is a sigil that causes a card bearing it to grant the player one Energy Cell when played. This increases the player's maximum energy by one, and immediately grants them one energy to spend.

name: Bees Within
text:
Rulebook: Once a card bearing this sigil is struck, a Bee is created in your hand. A Bee is defined as: 1 Power, 1 Health, Airborne.

Bees Within is a sigil which creates a Bee in your hand when a card bearing the sigil takes damage. This card will always create a Bee in the player's hand, regardless of whether the card is on the player's side of the field or their opponent's.

name: Bellist
text:
Rulebook: When a card bearing this sigil is played, a Chime is created on each empty adjacent space. A Chime is defined as: 0 Power, 1 Health.

Bellist is a sigil which causes a card to create chimes on each empty adjacent space when it is played. If an adjacent space is occupied, then a chime is not created there.  

If a chime created by The Daus is defeated by a direct hit, its attacker is immediately struck by The Daus. This trait is not retained if this sigil is transferred to another card.

name: Bifurcated Strike
text:
Rulebook: A card bearing this sigil will strike each opposing space to the left and right of the space across from it.

Bifurcated Strike is a sigil that bestows a card the ability to strike the spaces to the left and right of its opposing space (but not the opposing space itself), meaning that it attacks twice in a single turn.

Behaviour:
When a card bearing this sigil attacks, it strikes from left to right. If its first attack to the left of the opposing space causes it to perish, then the second attack does not happen. If this card is in the leftmost or rightmost lane, then it will not attack the left and right spaces respectively, meaning it will only attack once.

If a bearing this sigil also possesses the Trifurcated Strike sigil, it will override Bifurcated Strike. As of Kaycee's Mod V0.28, Bifurcated Strike and Trifurcated Strike now stack, resulting in 2 strikes to the left, 1 strike in the middle, and 2 strikes to the right.

If a card bearing this sigil also possesses the Sniper sigil, then the player will be allowed to choose two spaces to attack instead of one, and may choose to attack the same space twice. If a space occupied by a Repulsive creature is attacked, then only the attack on that space will be negated.

name: Blood Lust
text: When a card with this kills an opposing card, the card bearing this sigil will gain 1 Power. This power is removed after a battle ends, except specifically on the Hodag. This sigil is usually more useful on cards with higher Health, as it will have a better chance of having higher Power before dying.

name: Bomb Latch
text:
Rulebook: When a card bearing this sigil perishes, its owner chooses a creature to gain the Detonator sigil.

Bomb Latch is a sigil that, when a card bearing it dies by any means, allows the owner to select a card to be given the Detonator sigil.

name: Bomb Spewer
text:
Rulebook: When a card bearing this sigil is played, fill all empty spaces with Explode Bots.

Bomb Spewer is a sigil that creates Explode Bots on all empty spaces when a card bearing it is played. While this sigil is only obtainable in Act II, Mrs. Bomb's Remote from Act III has an identical effect.

name: Bone Dice
text: Bone Dice is an unused sigil that, when activated for 1 Bone sets the Power value of the card bearing it to a random whole number from 1 to 6.

name: Bone Digger
text:
Rulebook: At the end of the owner's turn, a card bearing this sigil will generate 1 bone.

Bone Digger is a Sigil which gives the player one Bone at the end of their turn.

name: Bone King
text:
Rulebook: When a card bearing this sigil dies, 4 Bones are awarded instead of 1.

Bone King is a Sigil that provides the owner with 4 Bones instead of 1 when the card perishes. This applies when dying under any circumstance: through sacrifice, combat or by more specific forms of death such as The Prospector's pickaxe and the effects of Steel Trap.

name: Bonehorn
text:
Rulebook: Activate: Pay 1 Energy to gain 3 Bones.

Bonehorn is a sigil that, when activated for 1 Energy, immediately grants the player 3 Bones.

name: Brittle
text:
Rulebook: After attacking, a card bearing this sigil perishes.

Brittle is a Sigil that causes a card to instantly perish at the end of the owner's turn, after it deals damage.

name: Brittle Latch
text:
Rulebook: When a card bearing this sigil perishes, its owner chooses a creature to gain the Brittle sigil.

Brittle Latch is a sigil that, when a card bearing it dies by any means, allows the owner to select a card on the field to be given the Brittle sigil.

name: Brood Parasite
text:
Rulebook: When a card bearing this Sigil is played, an Egg is created on the opposing space.|speaker=Rule Book}}

Brood Parasite is a Sigil added in Kaycee's Mod of Inscryption. When a card bearing the Brood Parasite sigil is played, a Broken Egg or Raven Egg card is created on the opposing space on the board (if that space is unoccupied). There is a 10% chance of a Raven Egg being spawned instead of a Broken Egg.

name: Buff When Powered
text:
Rulebook: If a card bearing this sigil is within a circuit, it gains 2 Power.

Buff When Powered is a sigil that causes a card bearing it to gain 2 Power, as long as it is inside a completed circuit.

name: Burrower
text:
Rulebook: When an empty space would be struck, a card bearing this sigil will move to that space to receive the strike instead.

Burrower is a sigil which causes a card bearing it to automatically move to block incoming direct damage in the vulnerable space.  

Behaviour:
When an empty space would be struck, a card bearing this sigil will instead move to that space and take the full damage. Unlike the Sprinter sigil, cards bearing this sigil can move from their current position to a new position regardless of any cards in between. This effect can trigger multiple times in a single turn, and if a card with this sigil is killed after moving to a new space, overkill damage can immediately be dealt to the card behind. If an opposing card with the Airborne sigil attacks, a card with this sigil will not move to block the attack unless it has Mighty Leap.

name: Clinger
text:
Rulebook: When one of your creatures is placed in a space, a card bearing this sigil will move towards them as far as possible.

Clinger is a sigil that causes cards bearing it to move to the closest space adjacent to any cards placed on the same side of the board. A card bearing this sigil can move through cards to do so, but will not end on the same space as another card and will not pass through the newly-placed card.

name: Corpse Eater
text: Corpse Eater is a Sigil which causes a card to be automatically played in the place of the first of the player's cards to perish by combat. The effect requires the card bearing this sigil to be in the player's hand.

name: Dam Builder
text:
Rulebook: When a card bearing this sigil is played, a Dam is created on each empty adjacent space. A Dam is defined as: 0 Power, 2 Health.

Dam Builder is a sigil which causes a card to create Dam cards on the spaces to the left and right of the card when it is played. If an adjacent space is occupied by a card, then a Dam is not created there. Dams adopt any other sigils from the card that spawned them, including those from Totems, potentially being extremely powerful because of this.

name: Dead Byte
text:
Rulebook: When a card bearing this sigil perishes, select a file. Place damage on the scales according to the file's size.

Dead Byte is a sigil that, when a card bearing it dies, allows the player to deal damage to their opponent by selecting a file connected to their computer. This sigil is exclusive to The Archivist boss fight, and cannot be applied to the player's cards.

Behaviour:
When a card bearing this sigil dies, all attacks are momentarily paused, and the player is prompted to browse through their computer to find a file. The player can see the size of their files by hovering over them, and the size of the file name provides a quick indication of how large the file is. When the file is selected, a weight is placed on the opponent's side of the scale: the larger the file, the larger the weight and the more damage that is dealt. The player cannot select the same file twice in the same fight.

name: Detonator
text:
Detonator is a Sigil that appears in Act II and Act III. When a Card bearing this Sigil dies, all adjacent cards (those to the left, right and front of the card) are dealt 10 damage. This effect doesn't apply for sacrificing a card bearing this Sigil, but destroying it with the hammer does activate the Sigil.

This sigil can be naturally found on the Explode Bot. In Act III, it can be given to a card of the players choice with the Bomb Latch Sigil.

name: Disentomb
text:
Rulebook: Activate: Pay 1 Bone to create a Skeleton in your hand.

Disentomb is a sigil that, when activated for 1 Bone, creates a Skeleton in the owner's hand.

name: Double Death
text:
Rulebook: When another creature you own dies, it is returned to life and dies again immediately.

Double Death is a sigil that causes all other cards that perish on the owner's side of the field to perish again.

Behaviour:
When another friendly card dies by any means (including sacrificing it or using the Hammer on it) while an instance of this sigil is on the player's side of the field, the dead card will be immediately resurrected and then die again. Each copy of Double Death on the board will add an additional resurrection, up to a maximum of 3 resurrections (4 deaths) if each other lane contains a creature with this sigil. If a card bearing this sigil dies, it does not resurrect itself, but it may be resurrected by other cards with this sigil.

Resurrecting a card counts as playing it again, triggering any on-play effects such as Rabbit Hole (an additional Rabbit will be added to the player's hand) or Battery Bearer (the player will gain an additional Energy Cell); Similarly, each death will grant additional Bones, along with triggering any on-death effects an additional time (An Unkillable card will grant another copy for each resurrection).

The dying card's sigils take priority before the effects of this sigil. If the dying card has a sigil which plays another card in its space when it dies, such as Frozen Away or Ruby Heart, the new card will be played in its place and the original will not be resurrected. If the death of a friendly card causes a card with this sigil to perish (such as if it is within range of a Detonator), then the card will be killed before the Double Death sigil can activate.

Each resurrection and subsequent death will increase the power and health of Ouroboros by 1, as well as adding more copies of the card into the player's hand, making this sigil an effective tool to quickly raise the card's stats if needed.

name: Double Strike
text:
Rulebook: A card bearing this Sigil will strike the opposing space an extra time when attacking.|speaker=Rule Book}}

This is a Sigil from Kaycee's Mod which allows a card with it to attack twice. This effectively gives the card more than 2 times the value, doubling its power and allowing it to attack an opposing card and Leshy. However, Stinky will make the Sigil less effective, and the card can take twice the damage from Sharp Quills.

This Sigil appears naturally on the Dire Wolf and Pelt Lice.

Notes:
- Mechanically, Double Strike adds an additional attack against the opposing space rather than doubling a card's attacks, effectively making a card having both Double Strike and Bifurcated Strike the same as a card having Trifurcated Strike.
- Similarly, a card with both Trifurcated Strike and Double Strike will strike the space to the left of the opposing space, the opposing space twice and the space to the right of the opposing space.
- If a creature with Double Strike attacks The Angler's Bait Bucket, the second strike will hit the Great White before it has a chance to submerge itself.

name: Energy Conduit (sigil)
text:
Rulebook: If a card bearing this sigil is part of a completed circuit, your Energy never depletes.

This article is about the sigil. For the creature, see Energy Conduit.

Energy Conduit is a sigil that causes the owner's Energy to stop depleting as long as a card bearing it is used to create a circuit. This does not increase the owner's maximum energy, but instead causes their energy to always be full regardless of any costs of playing cards or using Activated Sigils. This applies to all energy costs, regardless of whether they occur inside the circuit or not.

name: Energy Gun
text:
Rulebook: Activate: Pay 1 Energy to deal 1 damage to the creature across from a card bearing this sigil.

Energy Gun is a sigil that, when activated for 1 Energy, deals 1 damage to the creature across from the card bearing this sigil. This sigil's effect cannot be used to deal damage to the opponent directly but can be used to damage cards with the repulsive sigil.

It is exclusive to Plasma Jimmy.

name: Enlarge
text:
Rulebook: Activate: Pay 2 Bones to increase the Power and Health of a card bearing this sigil by 1.

Enlarge is a Sigil that, when activated for two Bones, will increase the Power and Health of the card bearing this sigil by 1 each.

name: Fecundity
text:
Rulebook: When a card bearing this sigil is played, a copy of it is created in your hand.

Fecundity is a Sigil which allows a card to create a copy of itself in your hand when it is played. Like other Sigils which trigger when a card is played, a card played via the Corpse Eater sigil's effect will trigger this sigil. This effect is stackable, meaning that if multiple Fecundity sigils are applied to a single card, then multiple copies of that card will be added to your hand when the effect triggers.

name: Finical Hatchling
text:
Rulebook: A card bearing this Sigil hatches when drawn if the numbers 1 to 5 are represented in the Health of creatures in your deck, and in their Power, and if there is a creature of each tribe in your deck.

Finical Hatchling is a Sigil that transforms a card into a Hydra when the player's deck meets certain criteria. This applies to any card that it is on, and not just the original.

name: Fledgling
text:
Rulebook: A card bearing this sigil will grow into a more powerful form after 1 turn on the board.

Fledgling is a sigil that allows a card to evolve, gaining Power, Health and/or sigils. At the beginning of the owner's turn, any of their cards bearing the Sigil will transform and will then generally lose this Sigil.

Behaviour:
Evolving will preserve any sigils transferred to the original creature by Altars, as well as any stat changes present before the transformation, such as permanent stat increases from Campfires or damage taken from enemies. 

By default, evolving a creature will add "Elder" to its name and increase its stats by 1 Power and 2 Health. For example, a 1/2 Bullfrog will transform into a 2/4 Elder Bullfrog. However, many creatures possess a unique form instead, or have unique properties to their transformation. 

If a card acquires this Sigil via the totem and has Unkillable, it will regain the Sigil and can be played again for an additional evolution.
- Cards naturally bearing the sigil always possess a unique form.
- The Wolf Cub transforms into a Wolf, gaining +2/+1.
- The Elk Fawn transforms into an Elk, gaining +1/+3.
- The Raven Egg transforms into a Raven, gaining +2/+1 and Airborne.
- The Strange Larva first transforms into a Strange Pupa, with no change in stats, then into Mothman, gaining +7 Attack and Airborne.
- The Sarcophagus transforms into a Mummy Lord, gaining +3/+1.
- The Dire Wolf Pup from Kaycee's Mod transforms into a Dire Wolf, also unique to Kaycee's Mod, gaining +1/+4, and loses Bone Digger in favor of Double Strike, also unique to the mod.
- The Tadpole from Kaycee's Mod transforms into a Bullfrog, gaining +1/+1, and loses Waterborne in favor of Mighty Leap.
- The following cards have a unique transformation, despite not naturally bearing the sigil.
- The Worker Ant and Flying Ant transform into an Ant Queen after 1 turn, gaining +0/+2, with the Flying Ant losing Airborne.
- Note that this is not due to the unique Power stat Ants. In fact, if an Ant Queen evolves, it gains 1 Power and 2 Health as per the standard rule.
- The Elk transforms into a Moose Buck, gaining +1/+3 and losing Sprinter in favour of Hefty.
- The Mole transforms into a Mole Man, gaining +0/+2 and Mighty Leap.
- The Mantis transforms into a Mantis God, losing Bifurcated Strike in favour of Trifurcated Strike.
- The following cards gain +1/+2 but have a unique name (as opposed to having "Elder" prepended to their name).
- Alpha transforms into "Omega".
- Child 13 transforms into "Child 14".
- Dams transform into "God Dam".
- Long Elk transforms into "Longer Elk".
- Opossum transforms into "Awesome Opossum".
- Mothman transforms into "Final Form". This appears to only be possible using a Totem with Fledgling, as well as a fully evolved Mothman returning to your hand with Unkillable.
- Great White transforms into "Greater White"
- Deathcards do not gain the "Elder" moniker and simply retain their original name.
- Curious Egg transforms into "Extra Curious Egg"
- The Bone Digger sigil will have its effect doubled, making it produce 2 bones instead of 1.

name: Frozen Away
text:
Rulebook: When a card bearing this sigil perishes, the creature inside is released in its place.

Frozen Away is a sigil which causes a new card to replace this card when it perishes. The card that spawns is unique, and depends on the card that originally bore the sigil. If a card that doesn't naturally have Frozen Away somehow gains it, an Opossum is created by default.

name: Gem Animator
text:
Rulebook: Mox cards on the owner's side of the board gain 1 Power.

Gem Animator is a Sigil present in Act II and the Finale of Inscryption. It appears solely on the Orange Mage. While a card bearing this sigil is on the game board, all  Mox Cards on the game board gain 1 attack power.

name: Gem Dependant
text:
Rulebook: If a card bearing this sigil's owner controls no Mox cards, a card bearing this sigil perishes.

Gem Dependant is a sigil that can cause the card bearing it to perish if there are no Mox cards on the owner's side of the board. This instantaneous death can occur at three possible times: at the start of the owner's turn (in the case of the opponent, before any new cards spawn), at the end of the owner's turn after all cards attack, and the moment the card bearing this sigil is played.

Note that, although this rarely comes into effect, this sigil requires the presence of Mox cards, not Mox Sigils. This means that, if a card that does not possess a Mox Sigil naturally has one transferred onto it (such as during the Act II Leshy fight), it cannot meet the conditions for this sigil, and so will not prevent any Gem Dependant cards from perishing.

name: Gem Detonator (sigil)
text:
Rulebook: When Gem Vessels on the owner's side of the board die, they Detonate (the creature opposing them, as well as adjacent friendly creatures, are dealt 10 damage).

This article is about the sigil. For the creature, see Gem Detonator.

Gem Detonator is a sigil that, as long as a card bearing it is on the field, causes all Gem Vessels on the owner's side of the field to act as if they have the Detonator sigil, causing 10 damage to adjacent and opposite creatures on death.

name: Gem Guardian (sigil)
text:
Rulebook: When a card bearing this sigil is played, all Gem Vessels on the owners' side of the board gain Nano Armor.

This article is about the sigil. For the creature, see Gem Guardian.

Gem Guardian is a sigil that, when a card bearing it is played, grants Nano Armor to all Gem Vessels on the owner's side of the board.

name: Gem Spawn Conduit
text:
Rulebook: Empty spaces within a circuit completed by a card bearing this sigil spawn Gem Vessels at the end of the owner's turn.

Gem Spawn Conduit is a sigil that, when used to complete a circuit, spawns Gem Vessels on any empty spaces inside the circuit at the end of the owner's turn.

name: Gift Bearer
text:
Rulebook: When a card bearing this sigil perishes, a random card is created in your hand.

Gift Bearer is a sigil that creates a random card in the player's hand when a card bearing it is destroyed.

name: Gift When Powered
text:
Rulebook: If a card bearing this sigil is within a circuit when it perishes, a random card is created in your hand.

Gift When Powered is a sigil that creates a random card in the player's hand when a card bearing it is destroyed inside a circuit.

name: Guardian
text:
Rulebook: When an opposing creature is placed opposite to an empty space, a card bearing this sigil will move to that empty space.

Guardian is a sigil that causes a card bearing it to immediately move in front of any enemy card that is played opposite an empty space. It is found on three cards naturally, being the Bloodhound, Bonehound, & Bolthound, all cards based off of a guard dog. If there are multiple cards with this sigil on the board, the left-most one will activate first.

Uses

Guardian has very few uses beyond basic defense & can actually get in the way if a card bearing the sigil moves to a space you didn't want it to. However, it has a few uses regarding combinations with other sigils:
- Mighty Leap can increase defensive capabilities with this card, allowing it to block creatures with Airborne.
- Touch Of Death makes use of it's ability to oppose new creatures & instantly kills them.
- Blood Lust is extremely useful when combined with this sigil as it allows a card to gain attack very quickly.
- In Act III, you can combine it with the Sentry and Touch Of Death sigils to prevent P03 from playing any cards from that point on.

name: Handy
text:
Rulebook: When a card bearing this sigil is played, discard your hand then draw a new hand of 4 cards.

Handy is a sigil present in Act II of Inscryption. When a card bearing this sigil is played, the player discards their entire hand and draws four new cards to replace it. If the player has less than four cards remaining in their deck, then the remainder of the deck is drawn. Note that in such a case, Starvation will only appear when the player attempts to draw at the start of the following turn.

name: Healing Conduit
text:
Rulebook: Other creatures within a circuit completed by a card bearing this sigil are healed at the end of the owners turn.

This Sigil is strange due to the fact that an image and a description exist for it, yet it remains unused. This sigil is also interesting because is is one of the 2 cards in Act II that are unused, but have an image. The other is Marrow Sucker, which is also used for healing. It seems the healing mechanic was never implemented, and it is unknown whether healing would increase maximum health, or simply heal them up to their max health.

name: Hefty
text:
Hefty is a Sigil which allows a card to move in the direction inscribed in the sigil at the end of the owner's turn, pushing any cards in the way in the same direction.

Behavior:
Rulebook: At the end of the owner's turn, a card bearing this sigil will move in the direction inscribed in the sigil. Creatures that are in the way will be pushed in the same direction.

The sigil can point to the left, or to the right, defaulting to the right when it is first played. If the arrow points to an edge, or points in a direction which has no empty space, the sigil will change direction before the card moves. If the card is obstructed on both the left and right (only possible if all lanes on the card's side of the board are occupied), it shakes and does not move.  

Cards bearing this sigil move after all damage has been dealt, with each card moving in order from left to right: for example, if two Hefty cards exist in the third and fourth lanes and both sigils point left, then the creature in the third lane will move left into the second lane, followed by the creature in the fourth moving into the third lane. This can lead to some unorthodox effects: if two Hefty cards bear sigils pointing left and exist in the first and second lanes, then the creature in the first lane will turn around and push the other creature to the right, with the creature in the third lane (originally in the second lane) moving left into the first creature, meaning that both creatures move back to their original positions.

name: Hoarder
text:
Rulebook: When a card bearing this sigil is played, you may search your deck for any card and take it into your hand.

Hoarder is a sigil which allows the player to search their main deck for any card and take it into their hand when a card bearing this sigil is played. If the player has drawn their entire deck, this sigil has no effect. The sigil cannot be used to draw from the side deck.

name: Hostage File
text:
Rulebook: When a card bearing this sigil perishes the file used to create it is really deleted from your Hard Drive.

For more info on how file selection operates, as well as strategies involving this sigil, see Captive File.

Hostage File is a sigil that, when a card bearing it dies, causes the file linked to that card to be "permanently deleted" from the player's computer. In actuality, this is simply a bluff: the file is not actually deleted, but a different, special file is created within the selected file's directory. This sigil is exclusive to The Archivist boss fight and the Captive File card.

Behavior:

Death:
When a card bearing this sigil dies, instead of deleting the file (as P03 claims), a text file is created inside the folder of the file in question named "[filename] DELETED.txt". The file, a message from P03, explains that it doesn't have the ability to delete files, but asks the player to delete the file themselves. If the file is moved out of its current directory (because it was deleted or otherwise), P03 will mock the player for expecting a "reward", and they will earn the Agonizing Remorse achievement.

name: Leader
text:
Rulebook: Creatures adjacent to a card bearing this sigil gain 1 Power.

Leader is a sigil that increases the Power of cards to the left and right of the card bearing this sigil by one. This is true even if the adjacent card is inanimate or does not usually attack, such as a Boulder or Gold Nugget.

name: Loose Tail
text:
Rulebook: When a card bearing this sigil would be struck, a Tail is created in its place and a card bearing this sigil moves to the right.

Loose Tail is a sigil which allows a card to evade a direct hit. When a creature bearing Loose Tail would be struck, a tail is created in its place and the creature attempts to move to an adjacent space. 

Behaviour:

General:
When struck, a card bearing this sigil moves to the right. If there is no free space to the right, it will move to the left instead. If neither movement is possible, the tail will not be created and the creature will take the hit directly.  This Sigil is only triggered by direct damage, meaning that threats such as Sharp Quills and Steel Trap will always affect the card directly. Each creature can only create one tail, though this will regenerate if the Unkillable Sigil causes the card to return to the player's hand. 

Tail Properties:

The tail generated will have 0 Power and 2 Health and can be sacrificed, with any Power/Health boosts acquired from campfires, Morsel or The Mycologists generally applying to the tail. Tails created will retain the tribe of the original creature while in play (excluding the Amalgam). If the Sigil is naturally found on the card, whether that be via the Skink or a Deathcard, it will inherit any additional Sigils added to the card through either events or the totem.

If Loose Tail is added to any type of Deathcard via the sacrificial altar, the resulting Tail will retain the original Deathcard's name and Cost, as well as adding its Power and Health to the tail's default stats. If a Deathcard is created with Loose Tail and Fledgling, it will drop a tail named "Greater [deathcard name]" if allowed to evolve to its stronger form before creating the tail.

Most tails simply take the name of the original creature with "Tail" appended. However, certain creatures create tails which have different names and illustrations. These variants are purely visual and do not differ in function.

name: Looter
text:
Rulebook: When a card bearing this sigil deals damage directly, draw a card for each damage dealt.

Looter is a sigil that allows the player to draw an extra card for every point of damage a card bearing this sigil inflicts directly on their opponent.

name: Made Of Stone
text:
Rulebook: A card bearing this sigil is immune to the effects of Touch of Death and Stinky.

Made Of Stone is a Sigil added in Kaycee's Mod of Inscryption. Cards bearing the Sigil are immune to the effects of the Stinky and Touch of Death Sigil. 

The Moon, The Limoncello and Boulder cards start with this Sigil.

Notes:
- The reason for this Sigil's creation and addition is likely purely to combat the ridiculous effectiveness of the Stinky and Touch of Death sigils against The Moon.

name: Many Lives
text:
Rulebook: When a card bearing this sigil is sacrificed, it does not perish.

The Many Lives sigil stops a card from dying when sacrificed. On certain cards, sacrificing the card enough times will cause it to transform.

name: Marrow Sucker
text:
Rulebook: Activate: Pay 2 Bones to heal a card bearing this sigil.
This Sigil is strange due to the fact that an image and a description exist for it, yet it remains unused. This sigil is also interesting because is is one of the 2 cards in Act II that are unused, but have an image. The other is Healing Conduit, which is also used for healing. It seems the healing mechanic was never implemented, and it is unknown whether healing would increase maximum health, or simply heal cards up to their max health.

name: Mental Gemnastics
text:
Mental Gemnastics is a Sigil in Act II and the Finale of Inscryption. The Blue Mage and Blue Sporemage naturally bear this sigil.
When a card bearing the Mental Gemnastics sigil is played, the player will draw cards equal to the number of Mox Cards on their side of the game board.

name: Mighty Leap
text:
Rulebook: A card bearing this sigil will block an opposing creature bearing the Airborne sigil.
 | speaker = Rule Book
 

Mighty Leap is a sigil that allows a card to block Airborne attacks: if an Airborne creature attempts to attack over a card with this sigil, this card will take the damage instead and no direct damage will be dealt.

This sigil is also notable for being automatically flipped to when the Rule Book is opened, as its page contains the code necessary for opening the safe in Act I.

name: Morsel
text:
Rulebook: When a card bearing this Sigil is sacrificed, ⁣it adds its stat values to the card it was sacrificed for.

Morsel is a Sigil that, when the card it's on is sacrificed, adds its power and health to the card it's sacrificed for. When interacting with special behaviours such as Ants, it will simply add the value of the Morsel card to the special behaviour. For example, if there are 2 Ants on the field, but one has been summoned by sacrificing a 1/1 Morsel unit, then that Ant will have 3 Power, which is one more than the special behaviour usually gives.

It has no special interaction with the Mysterious Stones event used to transfer sigils, stats won't be affected and only the sigil will be transferred.

This Sigil naturally appears on Mealworms, which only appear in Kaycee's Mod.

name: Mox Sigils
text:
Rulebook: When a card bearing this sigil is played, a (Green, Orange, or Blue) Gem is provided to the owner.

Mox Sigils are sigils that provide gems of the corresponding color to its owner. This allows to play any card needing the gem as currency, as long as the card bearing one of these sigils stays on the board. These sigils can only be found on Mox cards, and are key elements to the Magick deck. The Great Mox sigil combines the effects of the other 3 Mox Sigils, thus activating the 3 gems at once.

In Act III, when arriving in the West of Botopia, P03 will upgrade the Empty Vessels that constitute the Side Deck in this part of the game to bear these sigils. And although the gems they activate aren't used as currency to any card, they are able to boost the stats of any Gemified card : 

*Green Mox adds 2 Health.
*Orange Mox adds 1 Power.
*Blue Mox decreases cost by 1 Energy.

In Magnificus's part of the Finale, the Green, Orange and Blue Mox sigils can also be found in the side deck, as this one is made of Mox Cards.

name: Null Conduit (sigil)
text:
Rulebook: A card bearing this sigil may complete a circuit, but provides no effect.

This article is about the sigil. For the creature, see Null Conduit.

Null Conduit is a sigil that allows a card bearing it to complete a circuit without providing any additional effects. Although the icon does not directly appear on the card, Empty Vessels can effectively be upgraded to possess this sigil by travelling to the north-west area of the Act III map.

name: Omni Strike
text:
Rulebook: A card bearing this sigil will strike each opposing space that is occupied by a creature. It will strike directly if no creatures oppose it.

Omni Strike is a sigil exclusive to the final boss giants The Moon and The Limoncello, cards in Act I (in the case of The Moon) and Kaycee's Mod (in the case of both cards). A card bearing this sigil will strike each opposing space that is occupied by a creature from left to right, ignoring any empty spaces. If no creatures oppose it, it will attack the opponent directly in a single lane.

In early builds of the game, this Sigil used to be called Moon Strike.

name: One Half Bones
text:
One Half Bones is a variable stats present in Kaycee's Mod of Inscryption which causes a cards Power to equal half the Bones the player carries. When the player has an odd number of bones, the power is rounded down (e.g: 3 bones = 1 power). The Lammergeier is the only card to possess this trait.

This behaviour can be seen as similar to the Enlarge Active Sigil from Act II, which costs 2 Bones to use and increases the Power and Health of the card. Unlike Enlarge, however, the increase isn't permanent and changes depending on the player's number of Bones at any given time.

name: Overclocked
text:
Rulebook: A card bearing this sigil has increased power. But, if a card bearing this sigil perishes, it is permanently removed from your deck.

Overclocked is an Act III sigil that increases the Power of a card bearing it by 1. Any cards bearing this sigil that perish during a battle will be permanently removed from the player's deck when said battle ends. This sigil can only be applied by encountering the Overclock event on the Botopia map or bought from the shop after the Overclock event, denoted by a lightning bolt, at which point the player can choose to apply this sigil to any card that does not already possess it. This sigil does not prevent cards with Unkillable from returning to the player's hand, but will still remove them from the deck after the battle.

name: Power Dice
text:
Rulebook: Activate: Pay 1 Energy to set the power of a card bearing this sigil randomly between 1 and 6.

Power Dice is a sigil that, when activated for 1 Energy, sets the Power value of the card bearing it to a random whole number from 1 to 6.

name: Rabbit Hole
text:
Rulebook: When a card bearing this sigil is played, a Rabbit is created in your hand.

Rabbit Hole is a Sigil which creates a Rabbit in your hand when a card bearing the sigil is played. The Warren is the only card to naturally bear this sigil. Like other sigils which trigger when a card is first played, a card played via the Corpse Eater sigil will trigger Rabbit Hole's effect.

name: Rampager
text:
Rulebook: At the end of the owner's turn, a card bearing this sigil will move in the direction inscribed on the sigil. Creatures in the way will be thrown back behind it.

Rampager is a sigil which causes the card with it to move, similar to the Sprinter sigil. It has the added effect of switching places with any card in its way. This can be used to quickly move glass cannon cards such as Rattler out of the way of danger.

This sigil is found naturally on Wild Bull in Kaycee's Mod.

name: Repulsive
text:
Rulebook: If a creature would attack a card bearing this sigil, it does not.

Repulsive is a sigil which prevents opposing cards from directly attacking the card that bears it. It specifically only prevents attacks from cards, meaning the Prospector's pickaxe, the Trapper's Leaping Trap, Royal's cannons, recoil from a opposing card with Sharp Quills or other damage sources can still damage the card.

name: Ruby Heart
text:
Rulebook: When a card bearing this sigil perishes, a Ruby Mox is created in its place.

Ruby Heart is a Sigil present in Act II and the Finale of Inscryption. It appears solely on the Ruby Golem. When a card bearing this sigil dies, a Ruby Mox is left in it's place.

name: Scavenger
text:
Rulebook: While a card bearing this sigil is alive on the board, opposing creatures also grant Bones upon death.

Scavenger is a sigil that gives bones when an opposing creature is defeated. The card that has this sigil doesn't have to be the one who defeats an opponent as any creature defeated will give the player a bone, so long as said bearer remains on the board.

This is a unique sigil only found in Kaycee's Mod and on the Raccoon card.

name: Sentry
text:
Rulebook: When a creature moves into the space opposing a card bearing this sigil, they are dealt 1 damage.

Sentry is a sigil that causes a card to deal 1 damage to any creature that enters the space opposing it. This can include if the card is played in that space or moves to that space using a sigil such as Sprinter or Clinger. If a card bearing this sigil also possesses the Touch of Death sigil, this sigil's damage can also instantly defeat the opposing card if the attack is not blocked by Nano Armor.

name: Sharp Quills
text: Sharp Quills is a Sigil which makes the bearer deal 1 point of damage to an attacker of said card.

name: Shield Latch
text:
Rulebook: When a card bearing this sigil perishes, its owner chooses a creature to gain the Nano Armor sigil.

Shield Latch is a sigil that, when a card bearing it dies by any means, allows the owner to select a card on the field to be given the Nano Armor sigil.

name: Skeleton Crew
text:
Rulebook: At the end of the owner's turn, a card bearing this sigil will move in the direction inscribed in the sigil and drop a Skeleton in its old space.

This page is for the sigil from Act II. For the boss-exclusive card from Kaycee's Mod, see Skeleton Crew (Card).

Skeleton Crew is a sigil that causes the card bearing it to move in the direction of the sigil (in the same way as the Sprinter sigil), creating a Skeleton in its previous position. If the card is unable to move, then no Skeleton will spawn. This sigil shares similarities with the Squirrel Shedder sigil.

name: Sniper
text:
Rulebook: You may choose which opposing space a card bearing this sigil strikes.

Sniper is a sigil that grants a card bearing it the ability to select what spaces on the opponent's side of the field it will attack. If a card bearing this sigil has the Bifurcated Strike or Trifurcated When Powered sigil, the player will be able to select multiple lanes to attack, and may choose to attack the same lane multiple times.

name: Spawn Conduit
text:
Rulebook: Empty spaces within a circuit completed by a card bearing this sigil spawn L33pB0ts at the end of the owner's turn.

Spawn Conduit is a sigil that causes L33pB0ts to spawn in all empty spaces inside the circuit created by a card bearing this sigil when the owner's turn ends.

name: Spilled Blood
text:
Rulebook: The value represented with this sigil will be equal to the number of sacrifices made during your turn.

Spilled Blood is a variable Power stat, similar to the Ants variable stat. The value represented by this sigil will be equal to the number of sacrifices made during your turn. The Red Hart is the only card to possess this trait.

name: Sprinter
text:
Rulebook: At the end of the owner's turn, a card bearing this sigil will move in the direction inscribed in the sigil.

Sprinter is a sigil which causes the card bearing it to move once in the direction indicated by the Sigil when the owner's turn ends.

Behaviour:
The Sigil can point to the left or to the right, defaulting to the right when it is first played. If the arrow points to an edge, or another card, the Sigil will change direction before the card moves. If the card is obstructed on both the left and right, it shakes and does not move. 

Cards bearing this sigil move after all damage has been dealt, with each card moving in order from left to right: for example, if two Sprinter cards exist in the third and fourth lanes and both sigils point left, then the creature in the third lane will move left into the second lane, followed by the creature in the fourth moving into the third lane. This can lead to some unorthodox effects: if two Sprinter cards bear sigils pointing left and exist in the first and second lanes, then the creature in the first lane will attempt to move and fail, with the creature in the second lane turning around and moving right into the third lane, thereby creating an open space in the second lane.

Sprinter has a unique interaction with the Hefty and Rampager Sigils when it is added to a card. Cards that naturally bear either of latter Sigils that gain Sprinter will have their effect doubled. This can be used to strategic effect, such as using Rampager-Sprinter to narrow in on two lanes.

name: Squirrel Shedder
text:
Rulebook: At the end of the owner's turn, a card bearing this sigil will move in the direction inscribed in the sigil and drop a Squirrel in its old space.

Squirrel Shedder is a Sigil present solely in Act II of Inscryption, unique to the Squirrel Ball card. It functions similarly to the Sprinter Sigil, causing the card bearing it to move to an adjacent space in the direction depicted by the arrow on the sigil at the end of its turn, if the space is unnoccupied. Setting it apart from Sprinter however, when a card bearing this sigil moves, the place it previously occupied will be filled by a free Squirrel card.

If a card bearing this sigil runs into the edge of the game board or another card, it will attempt to turn around and move in the other direction, though this may become difficult due to the trail of squirrels left in its wake. 

Notes:
- Squirrel Shedder shares many similarities with the Skeleton Crew sigil.

name: Steel Trap
text:
Rulebook: When a card bearing this sigil perishes, the creature opposing it perishes as well. A Pelt is created in your hand.

Steel Trap is a Sigil possessed by Trap cards. When a card bearing this sigil perishes, any creature opposing it perishes as well; In Act I, this creates a Wolf Pelt in your hand. 

Behavior:
Steel Trap does not trigger Loose Tail and it will kill cards with the Repulsive Sigil like Ijiraq, as its effect is not considered a direct hit. If a card with this sigil perishes while no creature opposes it, this sigil will not activate. This effect activates immediately in the turn order, negating any overkill damage which its attacker may have been able to do to cards behind the trap.

name: Stimulate
text:
Rulebook: Activate: Pay 3 Energy to increase the Power and Health of a card bearing this sigil by 1.

Stimulate is a sigil that, when activated for 3 Energy, will increase the Power and Health of the card bearing this sigil by 1 each.

name: Stinky
text:
Rulebook: The creature opposing a card bearing this sigil loses 1 Power.

Stinky is a sigil which reduces the Power of the opposing card by one. If this causes the opposing card to have 0 Power, then it stops attacking entirely. This sigil cannot cause the opposing card's power to go below zero.

name: Swapper
text:
Rulebook: After a card bearing this sigil is dealt damage, swap its Power and Health.

Swapper is a sigil that causes a card bearing it to swap its Power and Health values when it takes damage.

name: Tidal Lock
text:
Rulebook: At the beginning of its owner's turn, a card bearing this sigil will pull small creatures, like Squirrels, into its orbit.

Tidal Lock is a sigil unique to The Moon, a card in Act 1. At the beginning of the owner's turn, the sigil causes Squirrels and Rabbits on the player's side of the field to be removed from play.

name: Touch of Death
text:
Rulebook: When a card bearing this sigil damages another creature, that creature perishes.

Touch of Death is a sigil which causes a card to kill creatures it damages in one hit. If the attack strikes the opponent directly, the sigil has no effect and the attack does damage according to its Power, as usual. If a card has 0 Power, it will not attack and this sigil has no effect.

name: Transformer
text:
Rulebook: At the beginning of your turn a card bearing this sigil will transform to, or from, Beast mode.

Transformer is a Sigil that appears in Act III of Inscryption. It allows a card to switch between its base version and a Beast Form, which corresponds to the Act I Beast Card of the same creature. At the start of your turn, a card bearing this Sigil will switch forms, gaining or losing Power and Sigils depending on the base card and the Beast Form it has. Note that no original Sigils besides Transformer will be kept in Beast Mode, however any modifications from Events will remain.

By default, there are three cards that naturally bear this Sigil: Son1a, Qu177 and Gr1zz. These cards have preset Beast Forms that they can transform into, transforming into a Bat, Porcupine and Grizzly with altered stats respectively. Additionally, you can give a card a Beast Form by using the relevant Event. At the Event, you will have three options for Beast Form that you can choose from:
*The Adder form turns the card to and from a 1 Power unit with the Touch of Death Sigil.
*The Wolf form turns the card to and from a 3 Power unit.
*The Raven form turns the card to and from a 2 Power unit with the Airborne Sigil.

name: Trifurcated Strike
text:
Rulebook: A card bearing this sigil will strike each opposing space to the left and right of the spaces across from it as well as the space in front of it.

Trifurcated Strike is a sigil that bestows a card the ability to strike the spaces to the left and right of its opposing space as well as the opposing space itself, meaning that it attacks three times in a single turn. 

Behaviour:
When a card bearing this sigil attacks, it strikes from left to right. If any attack causes it to perish, then subsequent attacks will not happen. If this card is in the leftmost or rightmost lane, then it will not attack the left and right spaces respectively, meaning it will only attack twice.

If a card bearing this sigil possesses the Sniper sigil as well, then the player will be allowed to choose three spaces to attack instead of one, and may choose to attack the same space multiple times. If a space occupied by a Repulsive creature is attacked, then only the attack on that space will be negated.

This sigil and Bifurcated Strike stack, resulting in 2 strikes to the left, 1 strike in the middle, and 2 strikes to the right. Additionally if a card possesses Trifurcated strike and/or Bifurcated Strike as well as Double Strike from Kaycee's Mod, the bonuses will stack, with all 3 allowing for a maximum of 6 strikes, 2 in each space.

name: Trifurcated When Powered
text:
Rulebook: If a card bearing this sigil is within a circuit, it will strike each opposing space to the left, right and center of it.

Trifurcated When Powered is a sigil that causes a card bearing it to effectively gain Trifurcated Strike as long it is inside a circuit.

name: Trinket Bearer
text:
Rulebook: When a card bearing this sigil is played, you will receive a random item as long as you have less than 3 items.

Trinket Bearer is a sigil which provides the player with an item when the card bearing it is played, as long as they have room for one. The item given is chosen at random, and all items except the Special Dagger, Fish Hook, and Failure can be received.

name: True Scholar
text:
Rulebook: Activate: If you have a Blue gem, sacrifice a card bearing this sigil to draw 3 cards.

True Scholar is a sigil that, when activated while the player has a Blue Gem, destroys the card bearing it in order to immediately draw three cards.

name: Unkillable
text:
Unkillable is a sigil that causes a card to return to the owner's hand after death.   

Behaviour:
Rulebook: When a card bearing this sigil perishes, a copy of it is created in your hand.

There are several unique properties to this sigil when combined with other sigils.

*Cards which change forms when sacrificed (such as the Cat and Child 13) return to the player's hand in their base form.
*Cards which grow due to the Fledgling sigil before they perish return in their grown form.
*If a card bears both this sigil and Corpse Eater, it is able to replace itself upon death.
*Since sigils transferred to a card also apply to any Tail cards generated by Loose Tail, this sigil allows the player to add a tail card to their hand.
*Similarly, sigils such as Rabbit Hole grant Undying to the resulting creature. Either this or the Loose Tail sigil combination can easily result in infinite sacrifice fodder and cards to block with.
*Since Dam Builder also transfers sigils to Dams it spawns, this sigil allows the player to add a dam to their hand.
*The Ouroboros has a special behaviour relating to this sigil: whenever any copy of it dies on any side of the field, all copies of the card have their Power and Health increased by one. This persists across all encounters and all three acts, but is reset between runs in Kaycee's Mod.
*In Act III, if the card has a beast alter-ego (that is, it possesses the Transformer sigil) and is killed in beast mode, it will stay in beast mode. That also works with the Overclocked sigil - the card won't perish and will return to your hand, although the card itself will still be removed from your deck after the battle.
*
*

name: Vessel Printer
text:
Rulebook: Once a card bearing this sigil is struck, draw a card from your Empty Vessel pile.

Vessel Printer is a sigil that, when a card bearing it is struck, allows the player to immediately draw a card from their Empty Vessel side deck.

name: Waterborne
text:
Waterborne is a sigil that allows the creature to be submerged for the enemy's turn, causing the opposing creature to skip over it when attacking. The only consistent ways to kill a Waterborne creature are either by doing overkill damage to it before it spawns or by getting it to attack a creature with Sharp Quills. 

Kraken Waterborne:

For tips on using this variant of the Waterborne sigil, see Great Kraken, Hand Tentacle, Bell Tentacle and Mirror Tentacle.

A special version of this sigil can be found on the Great Kraken. Though it misleadingly possesses the same description, it differs in that, when a card bearing this sigil re-emerges, it transforms into a random Tentacle card, losing this sigil in the process. If the card had any other sigils and was not the Great Kraken card itself, those sigils are also lost.

If this sigil is placed on a card which already has the regular Waterborne sigil, it has no effect. However, if the regular Waterborne sigil is placed on a card which has Kraken Waterborne (i.e. Great Kraken), it will still work.

name: Worthy Sacrifice
text:
Rulebook: Cards bearing this sigil count as 3 Blood rather than 1 Blood when sacrificed.

Worthy Sacrifice is a sigil that gives 3 Blood when a card bearing it is sacrificed.

name: Ant
text:
This article is about the trait. For the power stat, see Ants. For the creature, see Worker Ant.

Ant is a trait possessed by the Worker Ant, Ant Queen, and Amalgam, as well as Flying Ant in Kaycee's Mod. Cards bearing this trait are counted for the Ants Power stat; the number of cards with the Ant trait determines the Power of cards with the Ants Power stat.  The distinction between the Power stat and the trait is necessary, as Deathcards may possess the Power stat, but do not contribute to the count themselves, and the Amalgam contributes to the counts but does not have the power stat.

name: Uncuttable
text:
Uncuttable is a trait. Cards posessing the Uncuttable trait cannot be cut with Scissors, skinned by the Skinning Knife (in Kaycee's Mod) or stolen with the Fish Hook. Even though the Forced Death events in Act I summon many Grizzlys which are intended to be impassable, they are still cuttable.

Uncuttable cards: 
- Pack Mule
- The Limoncello
- The Moon

name: Satisfies Ring Trial
text: Satisfies Ring Trial is a trait possessed by the Ring Worm and Ouroboros. If player has no Ring, Cards bearing this trait will allow to pass Trial of the Ring when drawn.

name: Ants
text:
This article is about the variable stat. For the trait which assigns a card as an ant, see Ant. For the creature, see Worker Ant. 

Ants is a Variable Stat, representing the Power of certain cards. A card with this variable stat has Power equal to the number of ants on their side of the board. The Worker Ant, Ant Queen, Flying Ant, and Amalgam all qualify as ants, as they possess the Ant Trait.  

Deathcards with this variable stat can also be created if a card with the variable stat is selected for its Power and Health stats. (Note that such a Deathcard does not contribute to the number of ants, as it lacks the Ant Trait.) 

In the Trial of Power, Ants contributes 0 Power.

List of Ants:
Note that all Ants have the Ants Variable Stat representing their attack and Ant Trait.
- Worker Ant
- Ant Queen
- Flying Ant (Kaycee's Mod)

name: Card Counter
text:
Card Counter is a Variable Stat, representing the Power of certain cards. A card with this variable stat has Power equal to the number of cards in player's hand (even if card is on opponent's side of the board). The Hand Tentacle is the only card with this variable stat. 

Deathcards with this variable stat can also be created if Hand Tentacle is selected for its Power and Health stats.

In the Trial of Power, Card Counter contributes 0 Power.

name: Emerald Power
text:
Emerald Power is a variable stat, representing the Power of the Green Mage card. It takes the value of the number of cards giving a Green Mox currently alive on the owner's side of the board. This special behavior is only found in Act II, as the Green Mage can only be found during this act.

For a guide on how to use this Variable Stat, go to this page.

name: Bell Ringer
text:
The Bell Ringer symbol.
Bell Ringer is a variable stat which causes a card's attack stat to increase the closer it is to the combat bell, the value equal to the space number, plus 1 more for each Chime adjacent to it. The Bell Tentacle is the only card to possess this trait.

name: M!rror r0rriM
text:
M!rror r0rriM is a Variable Stat, representing the Power of certain cards. A card with this variable stat has Power equal to the Power of a card opposing it. If unopposed, Power equals to 0. The Mirror Tentacle is the only card with this variable stat. 

Deathcards with this variable stat can also be created if Mirror Tentacle is selected for its Power and Health stats.

In the Trial of Power, M!rror r0rriM contributes 0 Power.

name: Act I
text:
Act I is the first part of Inscryption. 

Gameplay:
The first Act takes place inside of a cabin. The Mysterious Figure / Leshy acts as the Dungeon Master of a roguelike style game where the player (represented by a figurine) moves across a map to reach their goal. There are four main locations represented on the map, the Woodlands, the Wetlands, the Snow Line, and the Cabin.

Every location has several split paths that one can take, with various Events presented depending on which path was chosen. Each path will lead to the location's boss: The Prospector for the Woodlands, The Angler for the Wetlands, The Trapper and  Trader for the Snow Line, and the Mysterious Figure as the final boss in the Cabin.

The main progressing beyond bosses consists of building and improving your deck throughout your run. The starter deck will always start the same except for the very first run.

The currencies for this act are Pelts and Teeth. Teeth are gained from doing overkill damage, and are used to buy Pelts.

name: Act II
text:
Act II is an 8-bit, open-ended version of Act I, where your goal is to defeat the four Scrybes.

Unlocking Act II:
These are the requirements to unlock Act II:

Obtain the Stunted Wolf Card and the Camera Film.
- To do this, you will need to unlock the Special Dagger (see page for more details).
- Use the dagger during a fight. When choosing a replacement eye, choose the bright blue one with symbols all over it. Your vision on the right side should now have a magic circle overlay (note, in order for the eye to appear you must have lost the game at least once).
- Hidden messages and marks are now revealed. Go to the clock and input the correct time.
- The secret compartment contains both the Stunted Wolf and the Camera Film. Grab both before you return to the table.

Defeat the Mysterious Figure.
- After defeating him, you will be brought to the cabin. However, you now have both the camera and the film.
- Quickly grab the camera, insert the film, and take his photo.
- You will now be free to move about the cabin.

In the cabin is the New Game option. Grab it and return to the menu. Act II begins when you begin a new game!

Gameplay:
Act II introduces two new mechanics - Mox and Energy - and many new cards. 

Act II uses Foils as its primary currency which can be exchanged with The Trader who appears in each area with the Scrybes. 

Act II also reveals that the Stoat was P03, the Stinkbug was Grimora, and the Stunted Wolf was Magnificus. The Mysterious Figure is named Leshy. These four are the Scrybes of Inscryption, and you, as the Challenger, are here to defeat them and take one's place. 

This Act ends with PO3 hijacking the game and taking control.

name: Act III
text:
Act III begins after P03 takes control of the game during Act II's finale. 

Gameplay:
Act III primarily takes place in a 3-dimensional P03's Factory. The player is, at first, restricted to P03's game board (Botopia, his own version of the world of Inscryption), but is later able to explore the factory and solve puzzles similarly to Leshy's Cabin in Act I.

Act III uses Robobucks as its primary currency. Holo-pelts are also available for the player to collect, but they are optional and not required for the game's progression.

Act III primarily uses the Energy mechanic, eventually introducing Mox. There are five card lanes instead of four during this act, and a Hammer which allows the player to destroy cards, much like its function in Act II.

The act ends after the player successfully defeats all four Uberbots and returns to the starting point of Botopia, before moving onto the Finale.

name: Blood
text:
Blood is a unit of Currency that can be used to play Beast cards, which are cards created by Leshy. 

In Game:
Almost any card can be sacrificed to obtain 1 Blood. If a creature is not a possible sacrifice, they will usually differ in appearance - such as having a dotted outline and a symbol with an X over a dagger in Act I or a darker background in Act II. Creatures with the Worthy Sacrifice Sigil are worth 3 Blood instead and can be used as sacrifices even when they ordinarily wouldn't.

You will only be prompted to sacrifice creatures when you attempt to play a card with a Blood cost of 1 or more. If there are not enough worthy cards to sacrifice to play a card, the game will prevent you being able to play it. Sacrificing removes a card from play, killing it and giving you 1 Bone. Creatures with the Many Lives Sigil, such as the Cat, will not die when sacrificed but will still give their Blood.

name: Bones
text:
Bones are an unit of Currency that can be used to play Cards that cost Bones. Bones are represented by Bone Tokens in Act I/Kaycee's Mod and the Finale, where they are placed in a pile to the left of the playing field from the player's perspective. In Act II, they are shown as a counter that counts up to 999 - though the total can be exceeded.

In Game:
Whenever a card on the players side perishes for any reason - whether it be from an attack, used as a sacrifice or due to a Sigil - they will receive 1 Bone. The only exception to this is if a card bears the Bone King Sigil, which instead yield 4 Bones.

Alternative methods to obtaining Bones are possible, either it be through using items or Sigils.
*Scavenger allows the player to gain Bones from enemy creatures whenever they perish. The number of Bones obtained per creature is increased for every instance of Scavenger in play.
*Bone Digger allows for natural Bone generation, with each instance of the Sigil generating 1 Bone at the end of the turn. When combined with the Fledgling Sigil, the evolved card will generate 2 Bones instead.
*Bone Lord's Horn in Act II has the unique Bonehorn Sigil, which converts 1 Energy into 3 Bones.
*The Hoggy Bank item gives 4 Bones upon using it.

Bones are used to play Bone cost cards. Whenever a card that costs Bones is played, the number of Bones required is taken from the player's total. In Act II, Bones can also be used to activate the special Sigils Enlarge and Disentomb. In Kaycee's Mod, Bones also contribute to the One Half Bones Power of the Lammergeier, where its power will be equal to half of the total number of Bones the player has at any time.

Bone Farming:
It is possible to farm Bones in a single turn in Act II using certain methods, which can then be used to play powerful cards or boost a card with the Enlarge Sigil to ridiculous levels for a quick victory.

The easiest method of Bone farming involves placing a Bone Lord's Horn inside of a Circuit completed by an Energy Conduit. Energy Conduits prevent the player's energy from decreasing. As the Bone Lord's Horn converts energy into bones, this setup essentially provides infinite Bones.

Another possible way to do this is more specific to a Bone deck, by combining a Tomb Robber and Necromancers. Use the Tomb Robber's Disentomb Sigil to summon a Skeleton, then use the Hammer on it to gain an additional Bone for each Necromancer in play (a maximum possible of three), allowing the player to farm infinite Bones. This method is slow, however, and more tedious.

The Boon of Goat's Blood is a Boon given to the player during Leshy's Trials in Act I of Inscryption. This places a Black Goat on the players side of the board for the final battle. This allows the player to play any card that costs Blood at the start of the battle.

name: Boon of the Ambidextrous
text:
|alt=]]
The Boon of the Ambidextrous is a Boon given to the player during Leshy's Trials in Act I of Inscryption. This boon allows you to draw twice at the beginning of your turn, from either deck. This helps heighten your chances of getting good cards from your normal deck, or can draw twice from your Side Deck to get more sacrifice outlets. However, this also helps drain cards, causing Starvation to come in quicker.

name: Boon of the Bone Lord
text:
|alt=]]
The Boon of the Bone Lord is a Boon given to the player during Leshy's Trials, or during the Bone Lord event if given a Black Goat in Act I of Inscryption. This boon gives the player 8 Bones at the start of all battles. This helps to easily play any bone card at the start of your turn.

This Boon does not stack and can only be acquired once, no matter how many Black Goats are sacrificed. You can however still get the Minor Boon of the Bone Lord, which works with this Boon. This Boon also cannot be acquired by sacrificing any creature with the Worthy Sacrifice sigil, as it must be a Black Goat.

name: Boon of the Forest
text:
|alt=]]
The Boon of the Forest is a Boon given to the player during Leshy's Trials in Act I of Inscryption. This boon places Grand Firs on all your spaces at the start of the final battle. This gives you a good amount of time to draw cards and plan for the next few turns, and if the trees are not destroyed by your 3rd turn, they will be turned into Gold Nuggets and provide further protection.

name: Boon of the Magpie's Eye
text:
|alt=]]
The Boon of the Magpie's Eye is a Boon given to the player during Leshy's Trials in Act I. This boon allows the player to, when drawing from their deck, chose any card from their deck to draw. This bypasses the randomness and risk of drawing from your deck, hoping for a powerful card. This mimics the Hoarder ability on the Magpie card, hence the name of the boon.

name: Boons
text:
Boons are special attributes given to the player during Leshy's Trials in Act I of Inscryption. Boons change the way the final battle works, giving huge buffs to the player. However, these boons do not carry over into your next run if you die. For each trial you pass, three out of the 5 boons will be offered, and the player may choose one. 

However, it is also possible to obtain boons in the Bone Altar event. It requires the player to sacrifice one of their cards, permanently removing it from their deck. If the card is a Black Goat, you will get the Boon of the Bone Lord in return. Otherwise, you receive a Minor Boon of the Bone Lord. (The Minor Boon cannot be earned from the trials.) If you choose to sacrifice a Pelt, you will instead recieve nothing.

name: Build-a-Card
text:
Build-a-Card is an event in Act III of Inscryption, first encountered in the southwest of the Resplendent Bastion, northwest Botopia. Similarly to the Card Recycle event, the player is prompted to pick a card from their deck to permanently destroy, but instead of gaining Robobucks, the player instead gains 'SP' to spend on making their own card from scratch in a point-buy system.

Recycling Stage:
The value of a card selected for recycling is based on the amount of changes the player has made to it.  All cards give 1 SP by default, and give an additional SP for each additional Sigil placed onto them (including Transformer and Overclocked). The source of the Sigil does not matter, however it is important to note that the Sigil must be added to the card. Sigils present on cards by default give no additional SP. The Sigil Power of the individual sigils does not influence the amount of SP given.

Gemifying a card also causes it to give an additional +1 SP.

The Most SP a single card can grant is 6. This is achieved by adding 4 additional Sigils to the card, and then proceeding to Gemify it. The only card that allows that is Gembound Ripper, since naturally present Sigils count for the 4 Sigil limit, but not for this event, and Gembound Ripper is the only obtainable card in Act III that by default has no Sigils.

Creation Stage:
The Creation stage is where the player may make their own card by spending SP gained from the Recycling Stage, as well as an additional +1 free SP. It is split into multiple segments in which the player sets various aspects of their card.

|-|Cost=
Cost:

The player may set the card's Energy Cost between 0 and 6 Energy. Each additional required energy grants +1 SP to be spent on the later steps.

The highest amount of SP that can be gained during this step is +6 with a cost of 6 Energy.
|-|Stats=
Stats:

The player may set the card's attack Power and Health. Each additional health point costs 1 SP, while each additional power point costs 2 SP.

The minimum amount of Health a card can be given is 1, while the minimum amount of damage a card may be given is 0. Both stats cannot be set higher than 9.
|-|Sigils=
Sigils:

The player may set up to 4 Sigils that they wish to appear on the card. Only Sigils with the MetaCategory Part3BuildACard appear as options. 

The SP Cost of any given sigil is equal to its Sigil Power, meaning that more powerful sigils cost more SP. Sigils with negative Sigil Power values grant additional SP rather than spending it. The only two available negative sigils are Annoying, granting +1 SP, and Brittle which gives +2 SP.

Sigils with a Sigil Power of 0 (namely Airborne and Detonator) do not cost SP to add to a card, but also do not grant additional SP.
|-|Appearance=
Appearance:

The player may set the card's appearance by cycling through various premade heads, bodies, and faces for their robot.

The player may set the name of the created card by cycling through various preset words as part of a three-part name.

name: Campfire
text:
The Campfire is an Event in Act I of Inscryption. The player meets five survivors gathered around a fire. The survivors invite the player to warm one of their creatures by the fire to make it stronger, but not out of any good faith.

Each campfire is capable of increasing either a creature's Power by 1 or its Health by 2.

Before the player's fifth run, their creature is automatically withdrawn after one buff. After this, the player can warm a creature by the Campfire several times, but each additional buff has a risk of losing the card. This risk increases the more the card is buffed, starting at a 22.5% chance on the second buff, a 45% chance on the third buff, and a 67.5% chance on the fourth buff. This allows increasing a single creature's Power by up to 4, or its Health by up to 8. 

If playing on Kaycee's Mod, you can only do this twice with the second buff risking a loss at a 50% chance.

If luck is not on the player's side, the survivors will eat their creature, causing a loss of the card. As compensation, the player is given a Hoggy Bank if they have room to carry it.

If the Ring Worm, Adder, or Long Elk is eaten, the survivors will be poisoned. They will be absent from all future campfires during the rest of the run, allowing one to achieve the maximum of four upgrades at no risk. Using a Custom Deathcard with Touch of Death or transferring the Sigil to another card and allowing it to be eaten will not result in the survivors' deaths. However, in Kaycee's Mod, any card containing the Touch of Death sigil will poison the survivors.

name: Card Battle
text:
A Card Battle is the term for a normal battle in Inscryption, taking place in all three Acts & Kaycee's Mod. Battles behave slightly different depending on the Act, but the core gameplay is the same.

Start Of Battle

When you enter a battle, you will draw 4 cards. In Act I, you draw three cards from your main deck & one Squirrel from your side deck. In Act II, you only have a main deck & draw 4 cards. In Act III, you draw 3 cards from your main deck & one Empty Vessel from your side deck. Your opponent will have 1-3 cards played in their lanes or back lanes, typically in their back lanes. When you ring the bell.

Turns

Every turn after the first turn, you draw one card from your main deck, or one card from your side deck. You then place cards on your side of the board, & when you are finished you ring the bell to end your turn. At the end of your turn, all cards on your side of the board will attack, the leftmost card striking first. When all of your cards are finished, the opponents turn starts. They play cards in their back lanes & the cards in their front lanes attack, with the leftmost card striking first. When your opponents cards have finished attacking, it's your turn again & the cycle repeats.

End Of Battle

A battle will end when the scales have been tipped 5 points in your direction or your Opponents direction. This is accomplished by cards striking empty board spaces.

Items

Items sit on the top right of the board, they may be used at any time during your turn & can be used in any order, but you can only hold 3 items at a time.

In Act I and Kaycee's Mod, there are multiple variants that have specific purposes. If the player has a Clover, they can swap out the cards offered for a new selection.
