name: Card Pack
text: Card Packs are a mechanic present solely in Act II of Inscryption, where they are the player's main method of obtaining cards. There are four different types of Card Pack corresponding to each of the four card types, Beast, Undead, Technology, and Magick. When a card pack is opened, it grants two random cards from its card type, one random rare card from its card type, and two random cards from other card types.

name: Card Recycle
text:
Card Recycle is an event in Act III that allows you to remove a card from your deck in exchange for Robobucks. All cards give 4 Robobucks by default, and give an additional 3 Robobucks for each additional Sigil placed onto them. The source of the Sigil does not matter, however it is important to note that the Sigil must be added to the card. Sigils present on cards by default give no additional Robobucks. The Sigil Power of the individual Sigils does not influence the amount of Robobucks given. Unlike Build-a-Card, Gemifying a card does not give any additional Robobucks.

The most Robobucks a single card can grant is 16. This is achieved by adding 4 additional Sigils to the card. The only card that allows that is Gembound Ripper, since naturally present Sigils count for the 4 Sigil limit, but not for this event, and Gembound Ripper is the only obtainable card in Act III that by default has no Sigils.

name: Cards
text:
__FORCETOC__
Cards are a critical aspect of the primary game mechanic. They have certain values of Power and Health and can bear Sigils.

Mechanics:

Most cards have a Cost before they can be played, although some can be played for free.  

When you end your turn by ringing the bell, the game enters the combat phase. All your cards on the field will deal damage equal to their Power to the opposing space on the opponent's side. The opposing card will then lose Health equal to your card's Power. If there is excess damage, the damage can overflow to another card behind your opponent's card. If there are no opposing cards, each point of damage will tip the scale toward your opponent's side by one.

After your cards' combat phase, your opponent will then play their cards (which are shown behind the space where they plan to play the card) and will enter their combat phase. Similarly, your cards will receive damage from opposing cards during this phase, and each damage point dealt directly will tip the scale toward your side.

Act I:
At the beginning of an encounter, you draw 3 cards from your deck and 1 Squirrel. The Cost of playing cards can either be Blood or Bones. Additionally, cards may have a Tribe.

At the start of your turn, you can choose to either draw 1 card from your deck or draw 1 card from your side deck, a Squirrel. You must draw before playing any cards or using any items. When you run out of cards in your deck, multiple Starvation will start to be played by your opponent. They slowly gain better stats and eventually the Airborne Sigil the longer you do not have cards in your deck. 

If you complete the third painting puzzle, all Squirrels will be replaced with Bees. In Kaycee's Mod there is a challenge that transforms Squirrels into Aquasquirrels.

Act II:
The player chooses their starting deck from the Scrybe they desire to replace. There are 4 types of cards: Beast, Undead, Magickal, and Technology. Depending on their choice, the player receives a variety of cards that are from the Scrybe they chose. The player can then curate the deck to their liking from cards found separately. 

Act III:
Similar to Act I, there are two separate decks: one with your deck and the other with Empty Vessels. However, Energy is now the main Cost of cards. Energy is replenished at the end of each turn. Additionally, it can be replenished during a turn with the Extra Battery item. 

How to obtain:

Act I:
There are many events where you may add or modify cards in your deck. These include:
- Campfire - Increase a card's Power by 1 or Health by 2 (one is chosen randomly at each encounter). You can do this up to 4 times each encounter (2 in Kaycee's Mod), with each additional buff increasing the likelihood of losing the card. You can also kill survivors once per run to make the chance of losing your card 0 for the rest of the run, if you lose a card that has Touch of Death naturally, a Ring Worm, or, in Kaycee's Mod, any card with Touch of Death at all.
- Deck Trial - Pass a chosen trial (out of three possibilities) with three randomly drawn cards to obtain a card with an extra inscribed Sigil. In Kaycee's Mod, cards have 2 Sigils inscribed.
- Mysterious Stones - Transfer the sigils of one card to another. Cards that have extra sigils inscribed upon them (from this event, The Trader, Deck Trial, or The Prospector) cannot be used at all in this event.
- The Trapper - You may use teeth to purchase Pelts to add into your deck.
- The Trader - You may trade Pelts in your deck for cards. The better quality the Pelts, the better cards you can obtain.
- The Mycologists - You may choose duplicate cards in your deck and merge them, combining their stats and Sigils into a single card. If your deck lacks any duplicates, the Mycologists will offer you 3 cards and you must choose one, all of which will be duplicates of any preexisting card in your deck, not accounting for Campfire buffs or extra inscribed sigils.
- The Prospector - Choose 1 out of 3 Boulder Cards. The Prospector will strike the card that you choose with his pickaxe, and either a Golden Pelt or a random insect card with a random additional sigil will be inside for you to take.
- Card Choice - there are four separate card choice events:
- Choose a card out of a pool of 3 random cards.
- Choose from a pool of 3 costs and receive a random card of that cost. The possible choices are 1, 2, or 3 Blood or Bones.
- Choose from a pool of 3 Tribes and receive a random card from that Tribe.
- Choose a card out of a pool of 3 random Deathcards.

After defeating each Boss, the player chooses 1 out of 3 Rare Cards to add to your deck.

Act II:
Primarily, new cards are from Card Packs, which you can either find around the world or receive after winning a battle. Booster Packs come in four varieties for each of the Scrybes. Opening a pack will give you 1 Rare card and 2 Regular cards from the corresponding Scrybe, as well as 2 additional cards from other randomly chosen Scrybes. Some individual cards can also be found across the map, and individual cards can be purchased from The Trader in addition to booster packs. New cards can also be obtained from The Mycologists.

Act III:
You can obtain new cards either from Events or the Shop. The exact cards offered will vary depending on which area of the map the player is in.
- Card Choice - Choose a card out of a pool of 3 random cards.
- Card Swap - Discard one of your cards, then select one of the 3 random cards offered as usual.
- Build-a-Card - Discard one of your cards, then create your own with its name, image, cost, Power, Health, and Sigils.

name: Circuits
text:
Circuits are a mechanic in Act II and Act III of Inscryption. A circuit is created when two conduit cards are placed on the same side of the board, causing various effects depending on what conduits create the circuit, as well as what cards are placed between the two conduits - referred to as powering those cards. Powered sigils have unique benefits when inside a circuit. If either conduit is destroyed, then the circuit is broken and all its effects cease.

Conduits placed within a circuit do not break the circuit, and instead receive the benefits of the circuit themselves while also adding their benefit to the circuit. For instance, if there are 2 Buff Conduits on either end plus a third between them, the new Buff Conduit will receive +2 Power while all empty spaces will give +3 Power.

name: Clover
text:
The Clover is a Non-consumable Item that can be used in Act I and Act II of Inscryption, as well as Kaycee's Mod. 

In Act I, it is obtained by completing the first painting puzzle. When brought to the table, Leshy will remark that the player must not like the cards he gives them; From then on, it can be used at various events to generate a new set of three cards to choose from.
- At a standard Card Choice node or a Deathcard Choice node, the clover will draw three new cards to choose from.
- At a Cost Choice or a Tribe Choice node, the clover must be used before selecting a cost or a tribe. It will generate a new set of costs or tribes to choose from, but the player still cannot see what creature they will get from each card; Selecting a cost or a tribe will remove the clover, and the player will be forced to take the card they turned over.
- The clover cannot be used during a Deck Trial, neither to choose a new set of trials nor to draw new inhabited creatures after a successful trial.

In Act II, the player can pick up the clover from the docks west of Leshy's woods. After collecting it, it appears at the start of a battle to the left of the player's hand, and may be used to redraw the opening hand if needed. Playing any card will remove it, and it may only be used once per battle.

In Kaycee's Mod, the clover is unlocked by default, and behaves identically to its appearance in Act I. However, the Cloverless Challenge Skull will remove it from the run, similar to its absence before it is unlocked from the painting. The first time that a Choice node is reached while this challenge is selected, Leshy will remark on its absence, wondering where he misplaced it.

name: Consumable Items
text:
Consumable items are special objects that can be obtained in Act I, Act III, and Kaycee's Mod of Inscryption. They sit to the right of the game board, and may be used at any time during combat, providing various beneficial effects to the user. 

In Act I, the player obtains multiple items along the path, and is able to hold a maximum of three. Act I items are lost permanently when used. 

In Act III, items are permanent additions to the player's game, and rather than being lost upon use, they must be taken to a Waypoint and recharged in order to be used again.

Item Sources:

Act I:
Throughout the run, items can be obtained at item draw events or via the Trinket Bearer Sigil. Additionally, solving puzzles or defeating bosses (namely, The Angler) can unlock items for future runs.

The Hoggy Bank item can also be obtained when one of your creatures is eaten at a campfire, as long as you have enough item slots.

Kaycee's Mod:
In Kaycee's Mod, all items from Act I are available (except the Special Dagger and Failure). There are also 3 additional items unlocked by completing the painting puzzle, and one that must be unlocked every run, from The Trapper for 7 teeth, and can then afterwards be obtained at Events. 

Act III:
Each item in Act III is obtained from a set area on the map/factory, and is obtained permanently once found.

name: Cost
text:
The Cost is the amount of a currency you need to pay to play a card. Some cards, like the Squirrel or the Geck, cost nothing. There are four types of costs, Bones, Blood, Energy, and Mox.

Blood is generally the currency with the most value per unit, followed by Mox, Bones, and finally Energy with generally the least (there are some exceptions).

Act I:
In Act I, the two cost types of cards are Blood and Bones.

Act II:
In Act II, all costs are used.

Act III:
In Act III, all cards cost Energy.

Finale:
In the first part of the Finale, cards cost Bones. As the second part is a reprise of Act I, both Blood and Bones are used. In the third part, Mox are used as the cost.

name: Deathcard
text:
A Deathcard is a Special card, referenced in Act II, but only usable or obtainable in Act I of Inscryption. They may be rarely obtained from card choice Events as well as their own special Event. They are additionally used in the Phase Two of Leshy's boss fight. If the Special Dagger was used during a run, that run's deathcard will be missing its right eye.

Creation:
When you lose, you will be prompted to select three cards, each randomly chosen from your deck. This excludes other Deathcards, Talking Cards and the Caged Wolf.
- The first card selection decides the Deathcard's Cost. (For example, if you select a Wolf the Deathcard will cost 2 Blood, or if you select an Opossum the Deathcard will cost 2 Bones.) Additionally, the cost of Pelts in your deck can also be selected, allowing the card to be played without any cost.
- The second card selection decides the Deathcard's Power and Health. Variable Stats such as Ants or Card Counter will also be copied.
- The third card selection decides the Deathcard's Sigils. If a card bears more than one Sigil (or has gained one by sacrificing another card), they will all be copied.
- If the player does not have enough suitable cards for any of the previous choices, Leshy will fill in the missing details for you. The default card is a 2/2 that costs 1 Blood, with no sigils.
- The last decision is the name of the Deathcard, which has no real effect on gameplay. This can be, at most, 16 characters long.

Finally, Leshy will take a photo of the player and set it as the portrait. The portrait depends on the head of the figurine that was used during the run, and is the only non-customizable part of the card. There are 6 eye variants, 6 mouth variants, and 8 head variants, resulting in 288 possible portraits. There are also another 288 possible portraits if you lose your last life while missing an eye (after using the Special Dagger), each missing their right eye.

You may then find the Deathcard in future runs.

Pre-made Deathcards:
From your second run onward, some Deathcards that were not created by the player may be found.
- Louis: a 1/1 that costs 1 Blood with the Sprinter and Waterborne Sigils.
- Kaycee: a 1/2 card that costs 1 Blood, with the Bifurcated Strike and Sharp Quills Sigils.
- Kaminski: a 0/1 card that costs 1 Bone, with the Guardian and Sharp Quills Sigils.
- Reginald: a 1/3 card that costs 3 Bones, with the Touch of Death Sigil.

Kaycee's Mod:

In Kaycee's Mod, Deathcards can no longer be created or obtained, but still show up during phase two of Leshy's boss fight. Additional premade Deathcards are used for it.
- Jonah: a 2/5 that costs 3 Blood, with Bees Within and Sharp Quills Sigils.
- Kevin: a 2/3 that costs 2 Blood, with the Rampager and Loose Tail Sigils.
- Sean: a 1/6 that costs 2 Blood, with the Mighty Leap and Touch of Death Sigils.
- Tamara: a 2/3 that costs 2 Blood, with the Hefty and Loose Tail Sigils.
- Daniel: a 2/2 that costs 2 Blood, with Double Strike Sigil.
- Cody: a 3/1 that costs 2 Blood, with the Burrower and Loose Tail Sigils.
- David: a 2/4 that costs 2 Blood, with the Hefty and Sharp Quills Sigils.
- Tahnee: a 1/3 that costs 2 Blood, with the Trifurcated Strike Sigil.
- Berke: a 2/1 that costs 2 Blood, with the Frozen Away and Guardian Sigils.

name: Deck Trial
text:
A Deck Trial is an event in Act I and Kaycee's Mod of Inscryption. The player arrives at the mouth of a cave, with a strange beast within who offers to join the player if they pass one of its trials.  

The player then chooses one of 3 trials to attempt. Trials are carried out by drawing 3 random cards from the player's deck. If the cards drawn meet a given condition, the trial is passed; if they do not, the player fails and the event ends. Note that pelts may be drawn.  

If the player succeeds, they are given a choice between 3 random creatures, each infused with a random additional Sigil. The randomly selected Sigil will never have a Sigil Power lower than 0 or greater than 5, to prevent negative Sigils from appearing. While there are no sigils with negative Sigil Power in Act I normally, Kaycee's mod introduces the Annoying Sigil with a power of -1, which is rendered incapable of appearing on rewards from the Deck Trial because of this check.  

In Kaycee's Mod, the cards rewarded will have 2 random Sigils infused instead of 1.

|Cards with no cost, or those that cost Bones, contribute 0 Blood.

|

|Pelts contribute 0 Power. Cards bearing Ants Power contribute 1 Power per ant (same as it works in combat). Tentacle cards contribute 0 Power.

As of Kaycee's Mod version 0.24, the Trial of Kin can be passed with 2 identical cards, even if they do not belong to a tribe.

- This is only after an update was released, meaning it could have been gotten earlier. This can be seen in Markiplier's playthrough of the game, where he mistakenly refers to it as "The Inhabited" as the actual name was just a single space.

name: Energy
text:
Energy is a Currency that can be exchanged for Creatures that cost Energy. Creatures that cost energy are usually robotic in nature.

Recharging:
Unlike Blood, Bones, and Mox, Energy is a Currency that automatically recharges. At the start of your turn, your Energy is replenished, and your maximum Energy is increased by 1 unless you are at the maximum of 6 energy.

Cards bearing the Battery Bearer Sigil will increase your current Energy and maximum Energy each by 1 when played, effectively reducing the amount of turns you need to achieve the a maximum of 6 Energy. If you already have a maximum of 6 Energy it will increase only your current Energy. If that is also at 6, then the sigil has no effect, even if the card it is on costs energy (the sigil's effect is calculated before the cost is deducted).

Cards bearing the Energy Conduit Sigil (the only such card being Energy Conduit) will keep your Energy at the current maximum, even when Energy is spent.

name: Extra Battery
text:
Rulebook: Replenishes Energy up to the current maximum. It's alright.

The Extra Battery is an Item in Act III of Inscryption. When used, it will refill your Energy to its current maximum.

The Extra Battery can be found alongside the tutorial path on the way to Central Botopia. Only one can be obtained, and if used a replacement copy will be given at a Waypoint.

name: Finale
text:
The Finale is the fourth and final section of Inscryption. It starts after Leshy kills P03, and Grimora starts the deletion process of Inscryption.

Grimora's Section:
Shortly after the deletion process starts, the player is transported to Grimora's Crypt.

Pre-Game:
The player starts in a small room, with a single tombstone blocking their way. After picking up and inserting three different epitaths, the tombstone sinks into the ground and the player may proceed to Grimora, who starts a game of Inscryption to celebrate the end of her life.

Gameplay:

Map:
The player moves their piece along a game board while Grimora occasionally moves two other pieces. Pieces cannot be moved diagonally, or pass over other pieces. Moving alongside one of Grimora's pieces initiates a battle. There is an interactable chest on the map that functions as a Card Choice event. The player is always offered a Bonehound, a Banshee, and a Revenant in some random order. However, the third choice gets deleted, forcing the player to decide between a random 2 of the 3.

Battle:
When starting a battle, the player draws 3 cards from their deck and a Skeleton. All cards cost Bones to play.

At the start of your turn, you can choose to either draw 1 card from your own deck or draw 1 Skeleton. You must draw before playing any cards. Your deck originally consists of 3 Gravediggers and two Frank & Steins, however you may choose to add one card to it through the card choice event.

If the player loses a battle, the section ends prematurely.

Boss Battle:
Grimora expresses with delight that she has enough time to do a boss battle, putting on a mask of Royal, setting up cannons along the board and playing loud music.

Despite the dramatic display, the boss fight abruptly ends before being properly started. The props for the fight get deleted, with everything else used to play following shortly after.

Ending:
After the game is unable to continue, Grimora and the player shake hands, and Grimora gets deleted.

Leshy's Section:
After Grimora is deleted, the player is transported to Leshy's Cabin.

Pre-Game:
Knowing the end is inevitable, Leshy opts to play one final game with the player.

Gameplay:

Battle:
The gameplay is identical to that of Act I. The player uses the same deck they did in Act I, minus any Talking Cards.

If the player would win or lose the battle, the scales get deleted and the game continues, with Leshy insisting they do not need to keep score.

As the battle goes on, more and more things get deleted. After the bell is deleted, everything remaining is rapidly deleted.

Ending:
After the game is unable to continue, Leshy and the player shake hands, and Leshy gets deleted.

Magnificus' Section:
After Leshy is deleted, the player is transported to the same blank white room Magnificus could be seen in during Act I.

Pre-Game:

The player must walk along a path full of broken pillars to Magnificus. If the player convinced Goobert to show Magnificus his painting in Act III, it will be along the path but with Goobert bleached out. Once reaching Magnificus, he attempts to convince Luke to eject the floppy disk, but he says that he has foreseen that Luke does not, and is doomed for his insistence. Remarking that they will both soon meet their makers, he initiates a dramatic final battle.

Gameplay:

Battle:
When starting a battle, the player draws 3 cards from their deck and a Mox card. All cards require Mox to play.

At the start of your turn, you can choose to either draw 1 card from your own deck or draw a random Mox. You must draw before playing any cards.

Instead of scales, there are health counters of 400, with whoever reaches 0 first losing.

As the battle goes on, more things begin to be deleted. Magnificus himself is almost deleted, but he resists it. Eventually, everything remaining gets deleted.

Ending:
After the game is unable to be continued, Magnificus continues to resist deletion, attempting to crawl towards the player to shake their hand. However, he is unsuccessful, and is deleted before he can reach the player.

OLD_DATA Section:
After Magnificus is deleted, the player ends up in an empty white area as the character they were in Act II. After travelling offscreen, the player finds the Woodcarver, who tells them there's not much left besides the OLD_DATA. She states you should not access it, pessimistically saying you will not listen to her, and then gets deleted.

After travelling offscreen two more times, the player finds the OLD_DATA. After unpacking it, numerous censored image files appear on screen while Luke Carder's heavy breathing is heard. It then cuts to Luke attempting to destroy the floppy drive with a hammer, the footage corrupting slightly every time he hits it, with the footage eventually cutting out.

The footage cuts back to Luke contacting Herman, a reporter, attempting to expose GameFuna for their malpractice. Before being able to properly provide his proof, Luke gets interrupted by a knock at the door. He angrily answers it, only for Amanda to shoot him. Amanda then proceeds to retrieve the floppy disk and leave.

The game then plays the credits.

name: Fish Hook
text:
Rulebook: To the user: Hook one of my cards and take it as your own. You must have an empty space on your side to receive it.
The Fish Hook is a consumable item in Act I. It allows you to pull one of your opponent's cards to your side of the board, placing it under your control. You must have an empty space on your side of the board in the same lane as the targeted card; if you do not, you cannot use the Fish Hook on that card.

This item mimicks The Angler's ability to pull your cards to his side of the board during his bossfight.

After defeating The Angler for the first time, you are given a Fish Hook at the beginning of each subsequent run. It cannot be obtained by any other means. In Kaycee's Mod, there is a challenge which removes the Fish Hook from the start of each run.

Uncuttable Trait:
Certain cards have the trait 'Uncuttable', rendering them immune to the Fish Hook. The name is in reference to the Scissors item, which shares this limitation. The two cards with this trait are the Pack Mule and The Moon, in addition to The Limoncello in Kaycee's Mod.

name: Foils
text:
Foils are the primary currency of Act II and can be traded with the Trader for Card Packs or Cards that match the area the Trader is in. They are obtained when a battle is finished with more damage dealt than needed to win. Every point of excess damage is converted to a foil, similiar to teeth.

*In Magnificus' Tower they sell Magick cards.

*In Leshy's Cabin they sell Beast cards.

*In Grimora's Crypt they sell Undead cards.

*In P03's Factory they sell Technology cards.

name: G0lly
text:
G0lly is one of the bosses in Act III of Inscryption. She is one of the four Uberbots created by P03, and represents P03 (hence her internet theme). G0lly can be accessed in the north west of Botopia, and is one of the two Uberbots (along with The Unfinished Boss) that the player does not have access to immediately without Rebecha repairing the bridge.

Boss Battle:

Phase 1:
At the beginning of the fight, G0lly will attempt to connect to the internet. She will then play a Mole card with the image of a real life mole. If the player has an internet connection, she will then start to play cards that have the name and profile pictures of the player's friend list with randomized Sigils and stats starting from the second turn. If the player does not have an internet connection or friends in their friend list, G0lly will play Mummy Lords with the image of a real life mummy instead.

On the third turn, G0lly will attempt to summon another online player's custom created card from the second phase. If successful, the player will receive that card and add it to their hand. If the player does not have an internet connection or G0lly is unable to find a creator online, she will instead give the player a Mummy Lord.

Phase 2:
At the beginning of the second phase, G0lly will begin by removing all cards in play entirely before prompting the player to create a custom card that will be used by another player. If the player who received the creator's custom card wins the first phase then the player who created the card will automatically win the second phase. 

If a custom card is successfully sent to another player, G0lly will inform the creator of the receiver's actions with the custom card. If the player who received the custom card fails, or if the creator is unable to find a receiver for the custom card, the creator is then given the custom card they have created. In this event, G0lly will then place another Mole along with 2 more Friends/Mummy Lords in the back lane. 

Personality:
G0lly is a rather innocent and curious Uberbot; probably the most childlike character in Inscryption. Her innocence is such that P03 dislikes it to the point of impossible metaphorification (See Trivia for its quote and Goobert's).

name: Game Limitations
text:
Act I Limitations:

Through the use of the Fecundity and Unkillable Sigils the player is able to create an infinite combo of buffing Ouroboros. Using this method, the player is capable of figuring out the following limitations.

Max Creature Statistics:
The maximum stat line of a Creature is 2,147,483,647 in both stats. This is due to integer overflow.

Act II Limitations:
The player is capable of creating a infinite combo in Act II using Bone Heap, Necromancer, Tomb Robber, and Skeletons. Using this infinite combo, the player is capable of figuring out the following game limitations.

Max Card Health/Attack:
There is virtually no maximum stat; however, over 999, the numbers will overlap with each other.

Max Bones:
While the amount of bones you have is virtually limitless, only 999 bones will be shown. If you have 1,000 and use one, the amount will not change from 999.

name: Gemification
text:
Gemification is an event in Act III of Inscryption that is first encountered in Gaudy Gem Land. The player will be prompted to choose a card, which will then become Gemified.

Unlike other upgrade events in Act III, Gemified cards do not gain a sigil. Instead, they gain symbols by their Health, Cost, and Power that each light up when a particular Gem is in play. A Gemified card will receive buffs depending on what Gems the owner has.
*Green Mox adds 2 Health.
*Orange Mox adds 1 Power.
*Blue Mox decreases cost by 1 Energy.

name: Grimora
text:
Grimora is one of the four Scrybes of Inscryption, the Scrybe of the Dead. She creates cards by noting tombstones' epitaphs with a quill on paper. She resides inside her crypt during Act II. 

Background:
's opening cutscene.]]
Grimora is one of the four Scrybes of Inscryption, being the Scrybe of the Dead and creator of the Undead deck. Using her quill, she inscribed the epitaphs of the deceased and turned them into cards for her deck. Grimora's ultimate goal is to assume control of the game, so that she may then use it bring it all down, thus ending the power struggle that she and the other Scrybes are locked in.

Grimora comes across as serious and concerned most of the time, but appears to have a mild sense of humor. She is excited for and eager for battles, often expressing it before a game begins. She even expresses her thoughts on having a chance to play a full game with Luke Carder during the deletion process. By contrast she is accepting of whatever role she is cast into by the other Scrybes' control, even when it is self-inflicted.

Act I:
Grimora appears in Act I as the Stinkbug. An unknown amount of time before the events of the game, she was turned into a card by Leshy and hidden within his safe. After she is released from her prison, she will be permanently added to the player's deck and occasionally give the player clues on how to escape.

Act II:
Act II Battle:
Grimora is fought as the boss of her area. In her battle, Grimora will only play specific cards that come back when defeated. At the start, she will play a Bonehound, before preparing to play a Sarcophagus and a Banshee. The Bonehound can be used to prevent one of these cards from entering play.

During this fight, each creature that you defeat will be given an epitaph (a quill notes it on paper). It will be written: 

*"R.I.P [name of the card]"
*"Turn [number of the turn it was put on the table] - [number of the turn it was destroyed]"
*"Death by [card that killed it or cause of death]"

When you no longer have cards, if the enemy's frontline is full of cards, one of them will be destroyed and replaced by a Starvation (the written cause of death will be "by accident"). If a Starvation replaces another Starvation, it doesn't trigger an epitaph.

When a creature is defeated, it will be resurrected 2 turns later, appearing on the enemy's backline.

At the start of the second phase, all of your cards on the table will be destroyed - the epitaph reading "RIP All your cards" "Turn 1 to Turn(number of current turn)" "Death by Grimora". - and then replaced in your hand as 0 Power and 1 Health, with the cost reduced to 0 while retaining any Sigils and abilities they had before. These cards will keep their names, but will have a withered appearance. Grimora will also prepare to play a Zombie.

After defeating her, Grimora will express satisfaction with her defeat and will request the player to spare her should they defeat all the scrybes. The player will then receive 2 Undead card packs.

Interruption:
Should the player have chosen to replace Grimora, she will appear sorrowful. She expresses great displeasure of being forced into a cycle once more. She comments that if it were up to her she would delete everything so that all of them can finally rest. She will ask the player who is taking control of Inscryption and soon after P03 will appear. She lambasts P03 before disappearing and P03 engages combat.

Finale:
After Leshy snaps the head of P03 off its body, the 3 remaining Scrybes meet again. Grimora uses the Archivist's folder to gain full access to the game files and deletes the contents of the floppy disk. Magnificus says that Grimora has doomed them all, but Grimora insisted that the deletion is freedom from all their strife and suffering. It fades to black before you end up in Grimora's Crypt, where you play cards with her.  However a tomb blocks the path with an empty slot and 3 nameplates with text that read "P03", "Inscryption.exe" and "Lucky Carder". You need to place these into the headstone to access the next area, similar to the puzzle to gain access to the Grimora battle in Act II. It does not matter what order you place them in, as the first two will always be deleted as you try to insert them, while the last one will remain and open the path to Grimora. 

Her map is unlike Leshy's, appearing as a chessboard with several pieces you can interact with in order to trigger her Events. Any card battles here will be played with her Bone gimmick, and use alternate models for the bell, scale, and other set dressing. 

She puts on a mask of Royal Dominguez and sets the theme when you get to the "Boss" of her board before it gets deleted almost right after she does. You shake her hand before Grimora herself gets deleted and you move on to face the next Scrybe, Leshy.

If you die at one of the other battles before that, however, it skips and ends the campaign prematurely.

name: Hammer
text:
The Hammer is a tool in Act II and Act III of Inscryption. It can be used on any card on the player's side, including terrain cards, dealing 100 damage to said card. If used on a card with Nano Armor, it will break the Nano Armor first. It will also activate any on death abilities, such as Latchers, Unkillable, and Detonator, assuming the card actually dies from the hit.

The Hammer can be seen inside Leshy's Cabin to the left side of the table, along with the Magickal Brush, however, both cannot be used and only vibrate when touched. When playing on console, pressing the left-most action button will cause the hammer to vibrate as it is the same button used to activate the hammer in Act II and Act III.

name: Harpie's Birdleg Fan
text:
Rulebook: To the user: Your creatures will attack as though they have the Airborne sigil this turn.

The Harpie's Birdleg Fan is an item in Act I of Inscryption. When used, it allows your creatures you have currently on the field to attack the opponent directly, similarly to how cards with the Airborne sigil attack.

name: Health
text:
Health is one of the two main stats in Inscryption. When being attacked, a Card's health drops equal to the Power of its attacker. When Health reaches 0, a creature dies and is removed from the match, going back to your deck if you were its original owner. When killed, creatures give you Bones.

Health will also drop to 0 instantly if the card is sacrificed, unless it has the Many Lives  sigil.

Some Sigils also interact with death, such has the Unkillable (which adds the card back to your hand when it dies) and the Bone King (which adds 4 bones to your Bone pile, instead of 1).

name: Hoggy Bank
text:
Rulebook: To the user: You will immediately gain 4 Bones.

The Hoggy Bank is an item in Act I of Inscryption. When used, you will gain 4 Bones.

Alongside the normal methods of obtaining items, a Hoggy Bank will be given when a creature is eaten at a Campfire, given that the player still has items yet to be filled.

name: Hourglass
text:
Rulebook: To the user: Your adversary will entirely skip their next turn.

The Hourglass is an item in Act I of Inscryption. When used, your opponent passes their turn, allowing you to take two turns in a row.

name: Kaycee's Mod
text:
Kaycee's Mod is an official expansion to Act I of Inscryption, modifying the Act into a repeatable roguelike with many unlocks and challenges. It is accessible from the main menu upon beating the game.

To unlock new content, the player must reach higher "ascension modes" by winning a run while enabling enough Challenges to fulfill each Challenge Point (CP) requirement. It is still possible to play with less CP than required, but no new content will be unlocked.

Accessing:
Before it was added to the main game, this mode was accessed via typing in "givemeascensionmode" as the beta key for Inscryption. Since being officially added, clearing the Finale is the only requirement. On PC, it can be unlocked early by using the key combination "Shift + K + M". After it is unlocked, a red skull card will be added to the main menu, allowing you to access Kaycee's Mod.

List of Changes from Act I:
- Tracked statistics, visible at the end of each run.
- 16 new unlockable cards, with 4 being Rare cards.
- 4 new unlockable Items.
- The Trapper allows you to buy their Skinning Knife for 7 teeth.
- Various new Sigils.
- 10 new Achievements.
- 15 different challenges; 11 of which need to be unlocked by playing the mode.
- 12 developer entries containing lore, although they must be unlocked by progressing through the mod.
- The Woodlands, the Wetlands, and the Snow Line appear in a randomized order.
- The Trapper will be weaker if encountered earlier, while The Prospector and The Angler will be stronger if encountered later.
- Only one additional buff can occur at the Campfire, carrying a higher risk of losing the card.
- Customizable map figurine.
- Leshy's Trials do not take place.
- By default, your starting deck consists of a Stoat, Bullfrog, and Wolf, along with two Rabbit Pelts that may be immediately given to The Trader.
- 7 additional Starter Decks may be unlocked.
- Several balance changes have been made compared to the base game.
- These are because, in the original game, certain cards were powerful because you were "meant to win" to progress the game. In Kaycee's Mod, the most powerful of these cards and sigils have been nerfed, the in-universe explanation being that Kaycee wanted to make a balanced game.
- Ouroboros is reset to 1/1 at the start of every run.
- Stoat has its stats reduced from 1/3 to 1/2.
- Cards created by the Fecundity sigil do not retain the Fecundity sigil.
- It is possible to sacrifice Terrain cards bearing the Many Lives or Worthy Sacrifice sigil (or the Mealworm sigil).
- Deathcards are no longer created upon losing a run and can only be found in Leshy's boss fight.
- Additional premade Deathcards are used for the fight, and any ones that you have created in the main game will not show up here.
- The Ring, Clover and Fish Hook are unlocked by default.
- A new event can occur starring Goobert and his painting skills.
- Most puzzles in Leshy's Cabin are disabled or altered. This makes the Special Dagger, Caged Wolf, Squirrel totem head, Talking cards and upgrades such as the Greater Smoke and extra candle unobtainable, as well as disallowing the collection of Teeth from the skull.
- The painting puzzle unlocks three new items, Magickal Bleach, Wiseclock and the Magpie's Lens.
- The Gramophone takes up Goobert's spot.
- The top door of the cuckoo clock displays a code when opened.
- The Safe reveals either a pile of rotting meat if the code from the regular game is inserted, or an extra record for the Gramophone containing songs from the game The Hex (a previous Daniel Mullins game) if the code found in the top clock drawer is opened.

Starter Decks:
In Kaycee's Mod there are unlockable Starter Decks, which you choose at the beginning of each run. By default, the player starts with 3 such cards and 2 Rabbit Pelts. After the Challenges are chosen, the game will let the player trade them with the Trapper. However, if the player manually ends a run in the first area, the next run will have one of the Pelt cards replaced with an Opossum. If they do it again, their last Pelt card will be replaced by a Ring Worm. This is a feature to prevent reset scumming. However, dying (even on purpose) does not trigger this effect. 

At first, the player will start with the Vanilla Deck but can unlock additional ones by reaching higher ascension levels. There is also a random dice button that will randomly select a starter deck from the unlocked decks.

First names specified are official names decks have (despite them never being shown in-game). Names after AKA is how community and other wiki pages may refer to them.
- "Vanilla" Deck:
- Stoat, Bullfrog, and Wolf
- "Moose Blood" AKA "High Cost Deck":
- Black Goat, Moose Buck, and Mole
- "Ants" AKA "Ant Deck":

- "Submersibles" AKA "Waterborne Deck":

- "Bones" AKA "Bone Deck":

- "Free Reptiles" AKA "No Cost Deck":

- All Totem Battles - 20 CP. All normal battles on the map are replaced with a random Totem Battle.
- No Boss Rares - 15 CP. Bosses award regular cards instead of Rares.
- More Difficult (two copies) - 15 CP. More cards with better quality (including stat lines and Sigils) from the opponent.
- Single Candle - 30 CP. You are limited to one life.
- Annoying Starters - 10 CP. Your starting deck's cards gain the Annoying Sigil from Act 3.
- Squirrel Fish - 20 CP. The squirrels from your side deck become Aquasquirrels.
- Grizzly Bosses - 50 CP. Switches the second phases of the first three bosses for 8 Grizzly cards with the Mighty Leap Sigil, similar to what happens in the regular game if you progress too fast.
- Final Boss - 20 CP. Leshy is replaced by Royal Dominguez as the final boss of the run, with his own mechanics and cards.
More information and strategies can be found on the Challenges page.

name: Leshy
text:
Leshy is a major character in Inscryption. He serves major roles in every section of the game, though most notably in Act I, in which he serves the role as the main antagonist.

Background:
Leshy is one of the four Scrybes of Inscryption, being the Scrybe of the Beasts. With his nature camera, he is able to take pictures of animals, turning them into cards. He can additionally use it on Challengers and celestial bodies. Leshy enjoys storytelling, and supplementing this, he uses masks in order to represent other characters. It at first appears that he is able to perfectly mimic the characters' mannerisms when donning their mask, but it becomes clear later in the game that he actually becomes those characters.

Leshy's greater goal is to simply play the card game forever, bringing others along with him despite their unwillingness.

Personality:
Due to his frequent acting, Leshy often portrays a more sadistic persona. When not playing a caricature of himself, Leshy is usually calm, although he is often angered when things don't go his way. He often talks as if narrating a tale instead of directly speaking to the player.

Relationships with other characters:
- It is unknown how Leshy feels about Grimora. He most likely dislikes her, as shown by his dialogue after she is added into the deck as a stinkbug. In turn, it's likely she holds a grudge against him for transforming her into a card.
- Leshy hates P03, both for its scheming and also its disdain for storytelling. His hatred is more than mutual.
- Leshy may fear Magnificus' planning abilities, as he removed one of his eyes and hid his card form more than the others. Magnificus despises him in return.
- It can be presumed Leshy cares for The Prospector, The Angler and The Trapper, as he made all of them Bosses when in control of the game. The Angler in turn shows strong devotion.
- Goobert's presence greatly annoys Leshy, to the point of trapping him inside a bottle and planning to throw him into the river.

Act I:
Leshy serves as the gamemaster and main antagonist. His visage is a mystery throughout the act, as only his eyes - and on occasion, his hands - can be seen by the player. He only reveals himself at the end of the act, both before and after fighting him. He has trapped the other three Scrybes in cards and hidden two of them in his cabin. He also has the New Game Card, which is kept in the locked storeroom near Magnificus' disembodied corpse. 

Boss Fight:
After reaching the final space on the map, Leshy will finally fight the player directly.

Pre-battle trials:
Before fighting Leshy, the player will have the opportunity to face Leshy's Trials in order to gain access to powerful Boons for the fight.

Phase 1:
Leshy plays Rare Cards during this phase, starting with a Mole Man in play. Additionally, at the start of his turn, he will alternate between doing one of two things:
- Put on a mask representing The Prospector, The Angler, or The Trader. The Prospector will always be first, followed by The Angler, then finally The Trader before looping back to The Prospector.
- If Leshy already has a mask on, he will perform a special action and then remove the mask:
- The Prospector: Destroy all cards on the player's side and replace them with Gold Nuggets.
- The Angler: Steal the most recently played card and move it to Leshy's side.
- The Trader: Play two cards with an extra infused Sigil, give the player one Wolf Pelt, and allow them to trade the pelt for one card on Leshy's side.

Phase 2:
After defeating his first phase, Leshy will put Grand Firs in front of Airborne cards, and Stumps in front of others. Cards with Bifurcated Strike are ignored. Leshy will play Deathcards during this phase, keeping the mask mechanic.

Phase 3:
After defeating his second phase, Leshy will turn around to face the moon and take a picture of it. He will then play The Moon, replacing all of his current cards. Once The Moon is destroyed, Leshy will marvel at the player's feat and invite the player to finish him off. No more cards will be played against the player after The Moon is eliminated.

Post-Battle:
After defeating him, Leshy will give the player a pile of rotting meat with a candle in it to celebrate their victory. Afterwards, he will blow out the candle, and the player will find themselves standing in the storeroom, with the camera on the shelf next to them. One of two outcomes may take place.

Outcomes:
Depending on whether or not the player has obtained the film roll, one of the following two outcomes will occur after picking up the camera:
- If the player doesn't have the film roll, Leshy takes the camera away from you and the player is prompted to make a special Deathcard. This Deathcard has the appearance of a Rare Card, with a red ribbon with the number 1 on it. It is unplayable with no stats, and the only thing that can be customized is the name. After finishing the Deathcard, Leshy will take a picture of the player. This results in them staying in Act I, with the 'previous challenger' hung on the door to your right for the rest of the act.
- If the player has the film roll, Leshy will attempt to take the camera away from you. However, the player succeeds in taking a photo of Leshy, and the player is allowed to take the New Game card to start Act II.

Kaycee's Mod:
Leshy reprises his role as gamemaster, although he lowers his narration frequency. He goes along with the various changes brought about, such as the randomized map order, or effects of challenges. In Kaycee's Mod, he seems less malevolent, though this may be a placebo effect brought on by Leshy's character growth through the game (which the player must have already beaten to play KCM).

Act II:
If the Beast Starter Deck was chosen, Leshy will attempt to teach the player how Blood works during their first battle, but he will stop after realizing they already understand. He will later explain how to use activated ability Sigils.

Leshy is found in his cabin, sitting at the table. When spoken to, he gives the player a camera to take pictures with and tells them to defeat his subordinates.

When spoken to after The Prospector, The Angler and The Trapper are defeated, he will engage in dialogue before initiating battle.

Battle:
Phase 1:
Leshy starts with a Stoat and Coyote on the board. When your creatures die in any way besides being sacrificed, Leshy will capture parts of them for use during Phase 2:
- First creature to die: Leshy captures its Cost.
- Second creature to die: Leshy captures its Power and Health.
- Third creature to die: Leshy captures its Sigils.

Phase 2:
After defeating his first phase, Leshy plays a Mole Man and the player's hand is emptied. Each lost card is replaced by the Amalgam created during Phase 1. If not enough cards died, he will fill in the missing details. He will play stronger cards than in Phase 1, including Grizzlies.

Post-Battle:
After defeating him, Leshy expresses sadness that things ended so quickly. He then gives the player two Beastly Card Packs.

Right after this, P03 enters Leshy's Cabin to taunt Leshy for his failure.

Ending:
If Leshy is chosen as the Scrybe the player wishes to replace, he will appear before them. He will angrily yell at the player for their actions, glitching out of the game shortly after P03 arrives.

Act III:
Leshy is seen hiding in the dredging room of P03's Factory alongside Grimora and Magnificus. There they urge the player to finish P03's game so it ignores the security cameras, with Leshy saying he will be the one to strike.

True to his word, Leshy rips P03's head off while it's uploading, killing it. Shortly after, against his wishes, Grimora begins the deletion of the game. Leshy expresses his worries before the player moves onto the Finale.

Finale:
After Grimora gets deleted, you are transported back in Leshy's Cabin. There Leshy decides to play one final game with the player, with them having the same deck as in Act I, minus any Talking Cards.

Leshy opens by playing a Coyote, then followed by a Mole, then a Bloodhound. Leshy may then play the Skink, Kingfisher, Mantis, Turkey Vulture, Elk Fawn, or Strange Frog.
During your second turn, the candlestick indicating overall lives is deleted. If the scale tips to either side, it gets deleted. Despite that, Leshy says that the two of you don't need to keep score and insists on continuing the match.

After enough turns, the bell will be deleted, with the cards and everything else on the table following. Leshy will give the player his goodbyes and shake their hand, only to be deleted as well. After this, the game moves on and you face the last scrybe, Magnificus.

Related Achievements:

Both of these achievements are gained through mandatory progression.

name: Magickal Bleach
text:
Rulebook: To the user: My cards on the board will lose all of their Sigils.

The Magickal Bleach is an item in Kaycee's Mod. When used, all cards on the opposing side of the board will lose their Sigils. Note that this does not affect cards that are yet to be played in the top row.

Unlocking the Magickal Bleach:
To be able to find and use Magickal Bleach, you must complete the first painting puzzle in Leshy's Cabin by placing the proper cards on your side of the board. Once done, the Cabin will shake and Magickal Bleach can be taken from the painting. Picking it up and bringing it to the table will add it to your current items, and make it possible to obtain in the future from item sources.

name: Magnificus
text:
Magnificus is a major character in Inscryption. He serves major roles in Act II and the Finale, and minor roles in Act I and Act III. He also has a major part in the console-exclusive ARG.

Background:
Magnificus is one of the four Scrybes of Inscryption, being the Scrybe of Magicks. Using his brush, he is able to paint his pupils as cards, immortalizing them as part of his deck. He can also use it to paint things only visible to his eyes without special equipment, and use Magickal Bleach to remove Sigils from cards. Magnificus is capable of some level of telepathic communication and has great foresight, able to create a plan for escaping Leshy's Cabin and predict P03's power play in Act II.

Magnificus' greater goals are unknown and are open to interpretation. Rebecha suggests that some of the theories are too terrible to speak of.

Personality:
Magnificus is generally polite in his dialogue, although similar to Leshy he is prone to fits of rage. In contrast to this, Magnificus can also appear anxious and desperate, being unwilling to accept his imminent death and attempting to bargain with and possibly guilt trip the player to spare him.

Magnificus appears to care very little about others, particularly his students by putting them through gruesome and often demeaning trials just to become cards in his deck. If he is ever displeased, he will see to remove them through any means possible - as he did with James Cobb. 

Relationships with other characters:
Magnificus expresses a disdain for Leshy and even more so for P03. Magnificus still holds a grudge against Leshy for excising his eye in Act I, referring to him as arrogant, single-minded and obsessed with power.

Magnificus expresses concerns regarding P03, and its intentions to perform The Great Transcendence, a plot that would extend beyond the standard power grab performed between the four Scrybes. For this, he considers it the worst Scrybe. However, he is willing to co-operate with it if the need benefits him. Not only is this shown in Act I, but it is also demonstrated in the ARG where he gives James Cobb over to P03 for his own purpose.

His relations with Grimora are less obvious. Forseeing P03's plot in Act II, Magnificus was writing a letter to warn only her about these actions, so he's willing to share some level of cooperation with her.

All of his students idolize him, particularly Goobert who goes so far as to paint a picture of himself with Magnificus. However, Magnificus does not appear to reciprocate these feelings, having bleached Goobert out of the painting. The Lonely Wizard also ends up distancing himself from Magnificus during Act III, stating that it no longer wants to endure the endless darkness that it was subjected to by the Scrybe.

Act I:
Magnificus mainly appears as the Stunted Wolf, however he still maintains a presence outside of his card form. The player must replace their eye with his as part of a mandatory puzzle, and if they are unable to complete certain steps of it after dying enough times, a cutscene will play with Magnificus giving a hint to the player.

Magnificus' corpse can be seen in the storeroom after defeating Leshy. His staff is also found on a wall of the cabin. 

Act II:
If the Magick starter deck was chosen, Magnificus will teach the player about how Mox works and how to use activated ability Sigils during battle.

Magnificus is found on the fourth and final floor of his Tower, looking outside the nearby window. When spoken to, he will engage in dialogue before initiating battle.

Battle:
Phase 1:
Magnificus starts with a Magnus Mox on the board and plays a variety of Magick cards.

When cards are drawn, Magnificus erases the colorless Sigils (all Sigils that aren't Mox) and replaces them with other Sigils using his brush. Cards without Sigils will also gain a Sigil. The Sigils that can be given this way are Rabbit Hole, Sharp Quills, Gem Animator, Ruby Heart and Mental Gemnastics.

Phase 2:
After the scale is tipped for the first time, Magnificus will affect his own cards in the same way he does the players at the start of your turn. The previous mechanic remains.

Post-Battle:
After defeating him, Magnificus attempts to warn the player about P03's plans, only to abruptly glitch out of the game. The player then receives two Magical card packs.

Interruption:
If Magnificus is chosen as the Scrybe the player wishes to replace, he will reappear. He expresses disappointment about the fact he has lost, glitching out of the game again after P03 arrives.

Act III:
Magnificus is seen hiding in the dredging room of P03's Factory alongside Grimora and Leshy. There they urge the player to finish P03's game so it ignores the security cameras.

After Leshy kills P03, Magnificus offers the player the New Game Card. However, before the player is able to click on it, Grimora deletes the game. Magnificus greatly disapproves of this action but appears to understand he cannot stop it, saying, "I'm afraid you've doomed us all, Grimora." Shortly after, the floor of P03's factory is deleted below the player and the Finale begins.

Finale:
After Leshy gets deleted, you are transported to a white void. There you find Magnificus. He attempts to bargain for his life, but admits that he knows it will not work, and also implies that Luke will die soon. He then decides to give the player one final duel, giving you a duel disk to play and draw cards, and uses life points of 400 instead of a scale.

Magnificus uses several of his cards from Act II, which remain unchanged mechanically aside from Mox cards forming the sidedeck. As the battle goes on, he chastises the player over the deletion of Goobert and erasure of the world. At one point, he appears to slow down time in the game, even affecting the rate of the deletion process itself, in order to paint one final time. However, when his canvas is deleted, time abruptly resumes its pace.

Eventually things start getting deleted like in the other Finale battles, only for Magnificus himself to abruptly become a target of deletion. However, he manages to resist it and continues the match. After it reaches a point where the battle is unable to continue due to deletion, Magnificus slowly drags his body towards the player to attempt to shake their hand. This is unsuccessful, being deleted right before your eyes. After he is deleted, the game becomes similar to Act II.

name: Magpie's Lens
text:
Rulebook: To the user: You will search your deck for any card and take it into your hand.

The Magpie's Lens is an item in Kaycee's Mod of Inscryption. When used, the player searches their deck for any card.

name: Minor Boon of the Bone Lord
text: The Minor Boon of the Bone Lord is a Boon obtainable through the Bone Lord event in Act I of Inscryption. It is given if the player sacrifices any card, excluding the Black Goat or any Pelts. One Bone will be given the player at the start of every round for each of this Boon obtained.

name: Mox
text:
Mox is a currency that can be used to play creatures that require Mox Cards to be played.

Gems:
There are three colors of Mox: Green, Orange, and Blue. Each of these has a gem associated with it. In order to play Mox Creatures, a Mox Card of the appropriate color has to be on your side of the field. Each Gem appears to be associated with a different style of play. Utilizing these play styles to their fullest can be useful in building a powerful deck. 

In Act II, Magick cards form the basis of the Magick deck. The majority of these cards either cost Mox to play or require Mox to stay active. There are also cards for each type of Mox, allowing play of other cards to be possible. In addition to this, some Rare cards give multiple Mox at once, making it easier to have a mixed Magick deck. The exact Mox the player requires depends on their intended playstyle.
*Green Emerald Mox cards are offensive, capable of achieving high Power values and being reliable units in most scenarios.
*Orange Ruby Mox cards are defensive, with high Health values that are capable of taking damage.
*Blue Sapphire Mox cards are supportive, focusing on aspects that aid the player at the expense of being neither offensive nor defensive.

Gemmification:
In Act III, in a special event, creatures can become Gemmified. Gemmified cards obtain the ability to change their stats whenever Gem Vessels are on the board. The player is able to change the type of Gem Vessel in their side-deck to suit their intended playstyle.
*Green Mox adds 2 Health.
*Orange Mox adds 1 Power.
*Blue Mox decreases cost by 1 Energy.

Gemmification can lead to some powerful synergies, and in some cases can make a card extremely strong. Depending on how the player has organized their side-deck, the exact benefits from each type of Gem Vessel will be different. Care should be considered when applying Gemmificated to a card whether the side-deck benefits it or not.

name: Mrs. Bomb's Remote
text: Mrs. Bomb's Remote is an item in Act III of Inscryption. When used, it deploys Explode Bots on every empty space.

name: Mycologist's Hut
text:
The Mycologist's Hut is an area in Inscryption's second act. Within it reside The Mycologists, who ask the player to give them sets of specific cards so they can experiment on them. These cards are Field Mice, Gravedigger, Sentry Drone, & Blue Mage.

Whenever you give The Mycologists a set of 2 cards they request for, they combine them into a special Spore variation of the card that has 2x the sigils that were originally on the card. These are Spore Mice, Sporedigger, Sentry Spore, & Blue Sporemage. And when you give them the 4 sets of cards, a special key will appear that is used in Act III to unlock the secret boss fight against The Mycologists. After you collect the key, you can continue to give them sets of cards that they request if you want more copies of any of the special Spore cards they make.

name: Nano Armor Generator
text:
The Nano Armor Generator is an Item in Act III of Inscryption. When used, it will give all cards on your side of the board Nano Armor if they do not already possess it.

The Nano Armor Generator can be bought from the shop for 26 coins. Only one can be obtained, and if used it will be restored at a Waypoint.

name: P03
text:
P03 is the main antagonist in Inscryption. It has major roles in Act II and Act III.

Background:
P03 is one of the four Scrybes of Inscryption, being the Scrybe of Technology. It uses a particle scanner to copy the CPUs of robots, creating Technology cards. As opposed to the finer methods used by the other Scrybes, P03 mass produces cards at a Factory, having an overflowing bin full of excess cards.

P03's greater goal is to perform 'The Great Transcendence', uploading the contents of the floppy disk to the internet and creating thousands of copies of Inscryption, with the hope most versions have P03 in charge. This plan was shown to have failed in-game, but after the ARG it was revealed it ultimately succeeded.

P03 comes off as arrogant and rude, often gloating when it wins and getting angry and blaming RNG when it loses. As shown in Act III, P03 does not care at all for story as opposed to gameplay, which it appears very skilled at crafting. This is likely in part due to its disdain for Leshy, who focuses mostly on storytelling.

Due to its personality, P03 is the most universally disliked Scrybe, with the others seeming to agree it's the worst of the whole group. Only its workers seem to care for it, but this is one-sided. P03 requests the player to tell The Inspector and The Melter to sacrifice themselves for better cards, and forces The Dredger to work overtime in search of OLD_DATA.

Act I:
P03 mainly appears as the Stoat, as its consciousness is trapped inside the card. Its 'corpse' can be seen in the storeroom after defeating Leshy.

Act II:
P03 is found in its Factory, but may first be encountered after defeating Leshy, where it will enter his Cabin to laugh at his defeat.

When spoken to at its Factory it will insult the players deck, then tell them to tell its workers to give it better robots, sacrificing themselves if necessary. After this the door to the inspection room is opened, and the player can proceed further in the Factory.

When spoken to after The Inspector, The Melter and The Dredger are defeated, P03 will express surprise and take back what it said about the players deck, then initiate battle.

Battle:
Phase 1:
P03 will play a variety of Technology cards, as well as Inspector and Melter, which are unique to its battle.

The gimmick of this boss battle is how the lower two rows function, which act like a conveyor belt, moving all cards clockwise at the start of the players turn. This will move cards from P03's side to yours over the course of the battle, and vice versa.

Phase 2:
When its first phase is defeated, P03 will scan your strongest card, then fill all of its empty spaces with copies of it. The copied cards will only carry the initial standard stats for that card, if their attributes have been improved with an activated ability, the improvements are not transferred.

The conveyor belt gimmick remains.

Post-Battle:
After being defeated by the player, P03 insults the Scrybe the player chose to replace (excluding itself), before giving the player two Techno card packs.

Interruption:
When the player selects a Scrybe to replace, P03 shows up. The Scrybe you chose will glitch and be transported away, and P03 will initiate battle.

Final 'Battle':
P03 will initially appear to be playing as normal, but it will soon play a card comprised of OLD_DATA. If the card is destroyed, P03 will make another copy. After one turn on the board, the card will corrupt the game and allow P03 to gain control of Inscryption, moving the game back to 3D.

Act III:

P03 serves as the gamemaster and main antagonist, bringing the player through a poorly distinguished replica of Inscryption's world. The player is initially cuffed to the table, preventing them from getting up, but when the power dies on the holographic tablet P03 uses to display the world, P03 lets them get up to fetch a new battery. The player is then free to explore P03's Factory, where it can be discovered that P03 has trapped The Angler and The Lonely Wizard in cards, and has also placed the New Game Card in a locked box.

P03's game, unlike Leshy's, has permanent progression. It presents the player with the goal of defeating the four Uberbots, all of which are initially shown as somewhat unflattering copies of their Scrybe counterparts.

However, this is simply a shell to aid its true motivation of performing The Great Transcendence with the unknowing help of Luke Carder, who took screenshots, gave it file access, connected it to the internet and finished the game.

It prepares to upload the game, but Leshy kills it, appearing to stop The Great Transcendence. However due to a video uncovered by the ARG, it is revealed The Great Transcendence succeeded. Part of P03's consciousness may also have been downloaded along with the release of inscyption.exe, as in the video, shortly after the game has finished downloading, the screen then shows the picture of the Stoat, which P03 was trapped in, it then briefly winks and cuts to black, possibly indicating that P03 survived somehow. 

Related Achievements:

All three of these achievements are gained via mandatory progression.

name: Pliers
text:
Rulebook: To the user: You will place a weight on the scales. The pain is temporary.

The Pliers are an item in Act I of Inscryption. When used, the player places one of their own teeth on the scales, earning a single point of damage.

name: Power
text:
Power is the amount of damage a card does per strike, indicated by the number in the bottom left of any given card.

Modifiers:
Power can be increased during a fight by adjacency to a Leader or by an opposing Annoying creature, or weakened by opposition to a Stinky creature.

For most creatures, it can also be increased for the duration of a run by Campfire or Mycologist Events. However, some creatures, such as Ants and Tentacles, have Power defined by Variable Stats rather than a static number, and thus cannot receive such buffs. They also count as 0 in the Deck Trial.

While the Ouroboros does have a numerical Power, its Special Behaviour allows this to increase by 1 each time it perishes, and the buff is permanent across runs as long as save data is not erased. 

See Game Limitations for the max Power stat.

name: Robobucks
text:
Robobucks are a form of currency used in Act III.

Unlike in Act I that uses Teeth and Pelts as currency or Act II that uses Foils, Robobucks can be used to purchase numerous things such as adding a Beast to a card, buy cards, create cards, and add sigils.

name: Royal Dominguez
text:
Royal Dominguez is a character in Inscryption. He serves minor roles in Act II and the Finale and acts as the final boss of Kaycee's Mod.

Background:
Born sometime in 1589, Royal Dominguez was one of the finest pirates of his age. Unfortunately, as common for his profession he ended up coming down with scurvy, which due to his lack of vitamin C, could not be cured. He eventually died of the disease in spring of 1632, at 42-43 years of age. His body was buried where Grimora's Crypt stands today, where he now serves as one of her ghouls.

Personality:
Despite being a stereotypical pirate, Royal does not act out any of the bad traits that would be associated with them, and he appears to be quite happy given his current state. He frequently makes jokes about the circumstances of his death and tells the player his past alongside the position of his tomb, alongside congratulating them upon solving Grimora's riddle.

Relationships with other characters:
Royal is never seen directly interacting with any other characters, but it can be assumed he has a level of devotion to his leader, Grimora. Grimora warmly returns this by fulfilling his truest dream of being a boss during the Finale, although this is unfortunately brief due to the deletion.

Act II:
Royal appears inside Grimora's Crypt, blocking the path to the mirror room. When spoken to, he will engage in dialogue before initiating battle.

Battle:
Royal's deck consists of a Ghost Ship and Skeletons. His primary strategy is to constantly bombard the player with Skeletons.

name: Rule Book
text:
The Rule Book is a glossary of useful information. By right-clicking on a sigil or item, the rule book is brought up and flipped to the relevant page with a brief explanation of the sigil's or item's function. The rule book contains explanations of all sigils, items, and boons. The player may flip through the book by using the A and D keys.

Act I:
In Act I, the rule book is placed to the left of the player in all battles once it has been accessed for the first time. 

The explanations for the variable Power Stats of the three Tentacle creatures are partially obscured with ink. 

The book contains the code to the safe (2-7-3) on the Mighty Leap sigil page. The Stoat instructs the player to find this code in order to free the Stinkbug.

Act II:
This act does not contain a rule book. Instead, descriptions of each sigil can be read by hovering the cursor over a card bearing that sigil, although they do not state the name of the sigil, and the description for Kraken Waterborne is the same as regular Waterborne, to confuse the player.

Act III:
In Act III, the rule book functions similarly to how it functions during Act I, the only differences being that it contains different sigils, no information on boons or variable Power stats (since neither exist in this Act) and has the appearance of a tablet to be more in line with Act III's technological aesthetic. When you finish a Build-a-Card event the rule book can no longer be accessed out of battles since it was placed on the conveyer belt and when Po3 sends the bot down the line, it pushes the rule book off the end of the conveyer belt.

Finale:
Although these sections are relatively short, both Grimora's and Magnificus' sections contain unique rule books, each with a unique appearance. These include listings of various sigils seen in previous acts but not available during these sections, as well as various sigils that do not appear anywhere in the game and are included either to provide the illusion of these sections being fully fleshed out experiences that are inaccessible to the player (e.g. Blood Guzzler and Haunter), or are included as jokes to amuse players who find their entries (e.g. Apparition and Virtual Realist).

name: Scissors
text:
Rulebook: To the user: You may cut up one of your adversary's cards. It is destroyed.

The Scissors are an item in Act I. They allow you to cut up one of the cards the opponent has in play, destroying it. The cards queued for play cannot be cut. If no cards on the opponent's side of the board can currently be cut, the item cannot be used. 

Like most other items, it can be obtained at a Gain Consumables event, or via the Trinket Bearer Sigil.  

Uncuttable Trait:
Certain cards have the trait 'Uncuttable', rendering them immune to the scissors. The three cards with this trait are the Pack Mule, The Moon, and The Limoncello.

Notes:
- Using Scissors on a Skink will create a Loose Tail in its place, even if the Skink has already dropped its tail.

name: Shop
text: The Shop is found scattered around the Act III map of inscryption, allowing the user to buy new cards and other upgrades using their spoils.

name: Side Deck
text:
The Side Deck is a mechanic present in Act I, Act III, and the Finale sections of the game. When the player draws a  card at the start of their turn, they have a choice between their main deck or their side deck. The side deck typically provides lower-cost, albeit less effective, cards compared to the main deck.

Act I:
In Act I, the player starts out with a side deck of Squirrels. They are guaranteed to start every combat with one additional squirrel in their hand, totaling ten costless cards available without using items. The squirrels can also be replaced by bees after solving the third painting puzzle.

Act III:
In Act III, the side deck consists of Empty Vessels. They later get upgraded to Gem vessels, which provide Mox as well. This side deck is the only one not to contribute directly to the cost system of the segment, namely Energy, although the Empty Vessels can be upgraded to have Battery Bearer.

Finale (Grimora):
In this segment of the Finale, the side deck consists of Skeletons, the only side deck cards who cannot block incoming damage, apart from the optional Kaycee's Mod Aquasquirrels. They cannot defend attacks, because the moment they attack they perish due to their Brittle Sigil. This does, however, mean that they generate Bones, which can then be used to play stronger cards. Skeletons are also the only side deck cards that can innately deal damage, excluding Bees.

Finale (Magnificus):
In this segment of the Finale, the side deck consists of Mox cards, Emerald, Sapphire, and Ruby. These are the only side deck cards that have 3 variants, excluding the Gem Vessels, but those are just upgrades to Empty Vessels.

name: Sigils
text:
Sigils are additional effects that can be possessed by certain cards. A card can bear multiple Sigils. The effects from these Sigils can be found in the Rule Book, or by right-clicking on a card's Sigil. Most Sigil effects are always in effect or occur automatically under predetermined conditions, though certain cards in Act II possess Activated Sigils that can be triggered anytime during the player's turn, as long as they can pay the necessary cost.

Note that some cards have symbols in place of their Power, which represent a variable number. For instance, the Worker Ant and Ant Queen have Ants power, which changes depending on the number of ants in play. These symbols are defined as variable stats and not sigils.

Some cards bear Sigils naturally, though all cards can obtain new Sigils through certain events.

Sigil Power Level:
Power Level is a hidden game mechanic present throughout the entirety of Inscryption. Every Sigil has its own Power Level, which can in theory be any integer, but in practice is never set lower than -3 or higher than 5.  Power Level is used to inform other mechanics about the general quality of a sigil.

It is worth noting that while many of the following effects from Act I use Power Level to exclude sigils with less than 0 power, there are no sigils with less than 0 power present in Act I. In Kaycee's Mod of Act I however, the Annoying Sigil is introduced, which has a power level of -1, which these checks serve to prevent its appearance on things such as totems.

Card Power:
Card Power is a number the game uses to determine various effects. It is largely informed by the sigil power. The Card Power of a given card is equal to the combined Power Level of all its Sigils, plus the value of its maximum health and the value of its power multiplied by 2 (e.g. 1 attack power adds 2 to the total card power).

Sigils with negative power, namely Brittle, Annoying, Gem Dependent, and Overclocked each lower the total power level of a card by their given negative values.

Effects:
- Deck Trial - Rewards granted by completing the Deck Trial are inscribed with a random additional sigil. This sigil is never of a power less than 0 or greater than 5.
- Totems - Totem bottoms will select a random player obtainable sigil between the power levels of 0 and 7. 
- This is done by picking a random number between 0 and 7.  Any sigils with a power level equal to or less than the random number are considered valid. The specific sigil is then chosen completely at random from the remaining candidates.
- In simpler terms, the totem will need to randomly select a number of 5 or higher to pick a level 5 sigil, and if the randomly selected number is 0, only 0 power sigils may be selected.
- The Prospector - The Prospector's Boulder Selection event has a 66% chance to provide the player with an Insect card bearing a random sigil. This sigil is never of a power less than 0 or greater than 5.
- The Trader - The Trader will reward you of a selection of 8 cards with one extra sigil if the player has a wolf pelt, and can take as many as they have wolf pelts.
- Bomb Latch / Brittle Latch / Shield Latch - Latch Sigils controlled by the opponent rather than the player will select the target of their latch via the Card Power of available cards.
- Skel-e-Latchers prioritise selecting the highest Card Power card the player has, while the others will target the highest Card Power card that the opponent has.
- Amorphous - The Amorphous sigil will not randomly transform into a sigil with less than 0 power or more than 5 power.
- Build-a-Card - The SP costs of various sigils during the Act III Build-A-Card event is equal to their Sigil Power.
- Bounty Hunters / Friends - Bounty Hunters are randomly generated using 'stat points' based on your current bounty level among other factors (see Bounty Hunter for more info). These Stat Points are then spent on sigils and stats for the hunter, with each sigil costing points equal to its power level. Friends use the same system of point spending, except the amount of points they have available to spend is based on the amount of turns that have passed in the fight against G0lly.
- Automatic Drafting - The Automatic Deckbuilding feature in Act II incorporates Card Power in its decision making process.

name: Skinning Knife
text:
Rulebook: To the user: You may skin one of your adversary's cards. It is destroyed and you draw a Pelt card.

The Skinning Knife is an item that The Trapper lets you buy for 7 teeth in Kaycee's Mod; it can also be obtained at bag nodes. It allows you to kill one of your opponent's cards, and gain a pelt for the remainder of the battle. Uncuttable cards, such as The Mule, The Moon or The Limoncello, cannot be skinned. The mouse icon used when you kill a creature with the Skinning Knife is the same one used when you want to sacrifice a creature.

name: Special Card Behaviours
text:
Special Card Behaviours are a hidden game mechanic. They are often confused with Traits, but unlike Traits, which serve as mere markers for other code and found on multiple cards, Special Card Behaviours have own code and usually are unique for a single card. There are 2 types of Special Card Behaviours - Variable Stats (for example, Ant or BellProximity), that dynamically update card's Power, and normal Special Card Behaviours (for example, Cat or TrapSpawner), that have more complex code and can create more sophisticated interactions.
