name: Special Dagger
text:
The Special Dagger is an item in Act I of Inscryption. When used, it adds a weight worth 4 points to the scale in your favor, at the cost of your right eye. Your vision will be impaired for the rest of the battle, but Leshy will let you choose a new eye when it ends. It is semi-unique, as while you can obtain it several times in a run, you can never have more than one copy of the Dagger at any given time.

The Dagger is a pivotal item for game progression: choosing the eye of Magnificus (the one with glowing green symbols on it) gives the player the ability to see, among other things, markings for the correct time to set the cuckoo clock to, earning them the Stunted Wolf card and the film roll necessary to complete Act I.

Note that Magnificus' eye will only be in the box once you are at least on your third run and you have lost at least once.

Unlocking:

*Get the Caged Wolf card from the third Wardrobe puzzle.
*Make the Caged Wolf perish by any means. The room will shake, and the cage around the wolf statue will be broken.
*Put the wolf statue next to the squirrel statue. This will cause it to release the Special Dagger.
*Grabbing the Dagger will add it to your inventory, and make it available at the beginning of every subsequent run, replacing the starting Pliers.

Related Achievement:

name: Starter Deck
text:
The Starter Deck determines what the player begins each section of the game with.

Act I:
The Starter Deck consists of a Wolf, Opossum, Stoat, and Bullfrog. After the player unlocks them, Stinkbug will replace the Opossum, and the Caged Wolf and Stunted Wolf will replace the Wolf.

The very first run has two Wolves, the Stoat, and River Snapper.

Kaycee's Mod:
The player can choose their Starter Deck before each run. Along with a three card deck, the player also starts with 2 Rabbit Pelts that can be traded at the first opportunity. 

See Kaycee's Mod for a full list of decks. 

Act II:
The Starter Deck depends on which Scrybe the player chooses to replace.
*Beast Deck: 20 cards7 Squirrels, 3 Stoats, 5 Warrens, 2 Adders, and 3 Hawks
*Undead Deck: 20 cards7 Skeletons, 3 Draugrs, 5 Gravediggers, 3 Zombies, and 2 Frank & Steins
*Technology Deck: 20 cards4 L33pB0ts, 4 49ers, 5 Automatons, 4 Thick Droids, and 3 Steambots
*Magick Deck: 20 cards3 Emerald Mox, 5 Mage Pupils, 3 Ruby Mox, 3 Sapphire Mox, 2 Junior Sages, 2 Mage Knights, and 2 Blue Mages

Act III:
The Starter Deck consists of an Energy Bot, Shieldbot, Sniper Bot, and Double Gunner. No alterations may be made.

name: Teeth
text:
Teeth are the currency of Act I and Kaycee's Mod. They are obtained when a battle is finished with more damage dealt than needed to win. Every point of excess damage is converted to a tooth. They can also be obtained from the skull in the Cabin, with the skull being refilled with 1-5 teeth at the start of a run and after defeating a boss; in Kaycee's Mod, the skull will never be filled with teeth. The Trader will also give the player 5 teeth if the player does not have any pelts with them or if they have a Pelt Lice in their deck.

Teeth can be exchanged for pelts at the "Buy Pelts" Event with The Trapper. In Kaycee's Mod, The Trapper will also sell their Skinning Knife for 7 teeth, but it can only be purchased once per run. 

The number of teeth the player has can be viewed beside the player's deck when out of battle, while trading, or on the pause menu (they will be displayed beside the icon for Foils). There is no limit to the amount of teeth the player may have, though if the player has too many teeth, they will not all be displayed when viewing cards or trading with the The Trapper. They will still be displayed in the pause menu, and the player will still be able to purchase items from the Trapper after all displayed teeth are gone, so long as they technically have enough.

name: The Angler
text:
The Angler is a boss in Act I, an NPC and opponent in Act II, and the Fishbot card in Act III.

The Angler is one of Leshy's subordinates. His role is that of a fisherman, his main task being to dredge Inscryption's files for OLD_DATA.

Act I:

Battle:
The Angler is the boss of the Wetlands. He has two phases.

Phase 1:
Unlike the other Act I bosses, the battle against the Angler starts with an entirely empty board. His cards in this phase include Kingfishers and River Otters. Additionally, as his special ability, he aims his hook at a card every other turn (denoted by a glowing hook symbol on the card). He always targets the newest played card, regardless of stats. At the end of his next turn, he will hook the targeted card, dragging it to his side of the field, pushing back any cards already in that space.  

If the player has not died at least once, defeating the first phase will result in the Angler filling the board with Grizzlies with the Mighty Leap Sigil.

Phase 2:
When his first candle is snuffed out, he clears his board and summons Bait Buckets in front of each creature in play. When a Bait Bucket is defeated, it summons a Great White. The only cards he plays in this phase are Bait Buckets.

Post-Battle:
After he's defeated, the player has their candles relit and proceeds to the Snow Line.

After defeating the Angler for the first time, the Fish Hook item is given at the start of subsequent runs.

Act II:
The Angler is seen fishing on a bridge outside Leshy's Cabin. He refuses to let you pass until he's shown a picture of a fish, after which he will initiate battle. Unlike most characters in Act II, he will speak without being interacted with before battling him.

Battle:
The Angler will always start by playing a Salmon, then another Salmon, and finally a Kingfisher.

Post-Battle:
After defeating him, he gives the player a Beastly card pack and allows them to cross the bridge.

He can also be found fishing at the dock after his battle. The Salmon in a chest there is likely one of his previous catches.

Act III:
The Angler has been transformed into the Fishbot card and hidden within P03's Factory. 

Kaycee's Mod:

Battle:
The Angler's Role in Kaycee's mod is roughly the same as in Act I, however he can be encountered later or earlier, as the map order is randomized in the mod. If encountered as the third boss, he will begin the first phase with 2 Bait Buckets on the board, and in the second phase he will forego playing Bait Buckets and play Great Whites.

name: The Archivist
text:
The Archivist is a boss that appears during Act III of Inscryption. It is one of four Uberbots the challenger must defeat in order to enact the Great Transcendence.

Behavior:
Phase 1:
The Archivist's main form of offense comes in the form of Librarians. When a Librarian is killed, the Archivist first asks for access to your hard drive, promising that no harm will come of this action. Interestingly, if you hover over "No", the No button swaps places with the Yes button, meaning that No is not really an option. You are then able to choose a file from your hard drive.

The size of the file you choose directly correlates to a weight on the opponents side of the scale that will be created.
- B: 0 Damage
- KB: 1 Damage
- MB: 2 Damage
- GB: 4 Damage
- TB: 8 Damage

Phase 2:
At the start of the second phase the player is asked specifically to choose a file that is "dearest to your heart, and one that shows age." The player is then made to choose a file to create a card (Captive File). The Power and Health of the card is dependent on the date the file was created. After the player has chosen a file, the Archivist will place it in your hand as a card, asking you whether or not the file was too dear to you. The card will contain the Hostage File sigil. The Archivist will then warn the player that if the card is destroyed the chosen file will be deleted from your disc. P03 assures you that it is completely serious.
- 0-359 days old: 1/1
- 360-719 days old: 2/2
- 720-1079 days old: 3/3
- 1080+ days old: 4/4

In addition to this, the field changes as well, from Gravestones and Librarians in the first phase to Dead Trees in front of all of your cards currently in play, as well as playing various cards from the Filthy Corpse World including Librarians.

Related Achievements:

name: The Mycologists
text:
The Mycologists are characters in Inscryption. They serve major roles in Act I and Act III, and a minor role in Act II.

Background:
The Mycologists are a pair of heads fused onto the same body, with the main head appearing to be a doctor, and the smaller head appearing to be a mushroom of some kind. They are not actual doctors or mycologists, but they are obsessed with experimenting on cards to figure out the Karnoffel code. They appear to possess some level of power compared to other characters, being able to infest Leshy's Cabin with mushrooms and remotely hijack P03.

Personality:
The main head appears nervous, frequently stuttering over their words and often relying on the smaller head to elaborate or finish its sentences.
The smaller head often speaks in short, blunt sentences, and despite its size, it appears to have more influence over the main head than the other way around.

During Act III, most of these character traits appear to be dropped, as the main head no longer stutters, and the smaller head speaks more clearly.

Relationships with other characters:
The Mycologists are never seen directly interacting with other characters, as they seem to be an independent force within the game.
In the console-exclusive ARG, however, P03 requested them to experiment on James Cobb so that it might be able to turn him into a card and NPC. So it is possible that they have some level of co-operation with the Scrybes, but how much and to what extent is unclear. It can be assumed they are quite knowledgeable about the Scrybes as well, being able to hijack Leshy and P03's campaigns.

Act I:
Event:
Mushrooms and an operating table with two slots for cards will appear on the table, and Leshy will don a mask of The Mycologists.

The Mycologists will offer to fuse a pair of duplicate cards, merging their stats and Sigils into one. For example, if the player has two Wolves, one of which is a 3/2 with the Airborne Sigil, and the other is a 4/2 with the Mighty Leap Sigil, The Mycologists will combine them into a 7/4 Wolf with the Airborne and Mighty Leap Sigils. Cost will remain unaffected.

Pelts can also be fused together, which can be traded to The Trader in exchange for fused cards replacing all the options for that kind of Pelt. For example, if the player has 4 Rabbit Pelts and fuses 2 together, they will be able to choose 3 fused cards from the 8 fused cards presented from The Trader, even though they only have one fused Pelt.

If the player doesn't have any duplicates, the Mycologists will give the player a random card that the player already owns. This can range from a Bullfrog to a Mantis God, however Deathcards, Talking Cards, the Caged Wolf and Ouroboros cannot be duplicated this way.

During card selection events, a small mushroom will appear next to any cards which the player already owns, indicating that selecting that card will give a duplicate.

After interacting with them, several mushrooms appear around Leshy's Cabin. They can be clicked to produce a sound but provide no gameplay effects.

Kaycee's Mod:
In Kaycee's Mod, the Mycologists act the same, although if you manage to get two Ijiraq and merge them, it may show that the stats have been added, but due to the peculiar nature of the placement of the card, the buff does not carry over when you play it. This is likely more of an unintended side effect than a bug, as the Ijiraq was not meant to be buffed.

They also have great synergy with Goobert's Event, as he will duplicate any of your cards, possibly with an altered infused Sigil.

Act II:

After defeating 2 Scrybes, The Mycologists can be found in their hut between Leshy's Cabin and Grimora's Crypt.

Duplicate cards may still be merged, but they will ask for specific ones in the following order:
*Gravedigger
*Field Mice
*Sentry Drone
*Blue Mage

When merged, these cards will turn into a 'Spore' form. While their stats remain the same, their Sigil will be duplicated and occur twice.

If the player wishes to quickly obtain the required cards, it is advised they farm Foils at the Training Dummy and 'cycle' through The Trader's inventory in each area by buying cards until the desired ones are found. The cards they ask for are always in the bottom left slot of her shop (except the Sentry Drone, who is in the top right slot).

Once the player has merged four pairs of cards, a key will appear, which can be used in Act III.

Act III:
The Mycologists can be encountered as a secret boss. This requires the player to discover a hidden path diagonally from the Eastern Botopia waypoint, and to have obtained the key from Act II. Upon unlocking the door and entering the room, the table fills with mushrooms before The Mycologists hijack P03, filling the factory with giant mushrooms and starting the battle. 

Battle:
Phase 1:
The Mycologists' side of the board changes both visually and mechanically. The 3rd space gains a symbol on it, and the other 4 spaces gain arrows pointing towards it.

At the start of the player's turn, their cards on the 2nd and 4th space will fuse into a new card on the 3rd space, and all cards on the 1st and 5th space will move to the 2nd and 4th spaces respectively. The fused card will have all the Sigils and combined stats of all cards merged into it. If a card is already present on the 3rd space, it will have the cards merged into it, further enhancing its stats.

Phase II:
After beating their first phase, The Mycologists remove all cards from their side of the board and fuse all the players cards in the same way theirs were, then play and fuse an Explode Bot and an Alarm Bot.

For the rest of the fight, cards on both sides of the board will fuse together in the way previously described.

Post-Battle:
After the player wins, the Mycologists merge a Gem Detonator with The Daus into a fragment of the OLD_DATA, which they take before disappearing, leaving P03 confused about what happened. If the player had a surviving merged card, it is added to their deck as a Mycobot.

name: The Photographer
text:
The Photographer is a boss in Act III of Inscryption. It is one of the four Uberbots created by P03, and represents Leshy (hence its camera theme). The Photographer can be accessed in the north east of Botopia, and is one of the two Uberbots (along with the Archivist) that the player has access to immediately without needing Rebecha to repair the bridge.

Behavior:
The Photographer (due to the nature of its Photography gimmick) has extremely punishing attacks, playing five Shutterbugs on its second turn. The player may be able to overcome it without utilising photography, but it is unlikely and not recommended.

At the beginning of its second phase, The Photographer will place Ancient Firs on all but one of the five available lanes, though this is not accompanied by any notable change in behaviour.

Photography:
The Photographer is accompanied by a Camera Drone. At the end of each turn, the player will be allowed to take a photograph of the battlefield using this drone (though this is not mandatory, and they may choose to pass). Alternatively, if a photograph has already been taken, the player is given the option to revert the game board to the state depicted in the photograph. 

This reversion affects card placement, positions, and statistics of both the player's cards and cards belonging to the Photographer, but it does not affect damage that has already been placed on the scales, nor does it affect items that have been used.

The player may not revert to the same photograph more than once, as the photograph is deleted once the reversion is complete.

Related Achievements:

name: The Prospector
text:
The Prospector is an NPC and boss in Act I, an NPC and opponent in Act II, and an NPC in Act III.

He is one of Leshy's subordinates. He keeps a monstrously large Bloodhound as a pet, which he loves dearly.
Act I:
Event:
This event will only occur in the Woodlands in the base game if player had completed at least 3 runs and had defeated The Prospector at least once. The Prospector will place 3 Boulders on the table and ask the player to pick one for him to strike. After this he will break it open, and the player will keep whichever card is found inside.

The cards obtainable are:
- (66%) A random unlocked Insect card with a random additional Sigil. This card cannot be a Ring Worm, or Bee, however.
- (33%) A Golden Pelt.

Boss Fight:
The Prospector is the boss of the Woodlands. He has two phases.  

Phase 1:
In his first phase, the Prospector always starts with his Pack Mule and a Coyote, otherwise playing an assortment of cards.  

Phase 2:
After you trigger his second phase, the Prospector will use his pickaxe to kill all of your cards on the table, replacing them with Gold Nuggets. He will then play a Bloodhound. 

Post-Battle:
After he's defeated, the player has their candles relit and proceeds to the Wetlands.
Act II:
The Prospector appears outside Leshy's Cabin, standing in front of the path to the pond. He will refuse to let the player pass until shown a picture of his Bloodhound, after which he will initiate battle.

Battle:
The Prospector starts by playing a Squirrel, and then a Bloodhound. He then plays a Coyote and Wolf Cub in a random order.

Post-Battle:
After defeating him, he gives the player a Beastly card pack and hops onto the rocks, allowing them to go to the pond.

Act III:
The Prospector is an NPC in Foul Backwater, seemingly being turned into a robot. His only role is to clear a shortcut for the player, after which he disappears.

Kaycee's Mod:

Event:
The event is exactly the same as in Act I, but it can occur in any map region if The Prospector has not been previously defeated or encountered in the run.

Battle:
The Prospector's Role in Kaycee's mod is roughly the same as in Act I, however he can be encountered later, as the map order is randomized in the mod. If encountered as the second or third boss, he will play more powerful cards such as Wolves. In his second phase, his Bloodhound gains a sigil such as Touch of Death or Bifurcated Strike.

name: The Trader
text:
The Trader is an NPC and boss in Act I, and an NPC in Act II and Act III.

She is an odd-looking woman who trades cards for Pelts or Foils. She and the Trapper are the same person, with her seemingly being the main, calmer personality of the two.

Act I:
Event:
When encountered, the Trader will allow trading Pelts obtained from the Trapper for different cards depending on their type:

Pelts that are merged by the Mycologists replace all cards of their type with merged cards, even if only one of the Pelts is merged. This can allow the player to obtain large amounts of powerful cards if they purchase several Wolf or Golden Pelts and merge just one pair, however one must keep in mind so many Pelts will take up a lot of space in their deck.

If the player does not have any pelts, the trapper will chastise the player and give them 5 golden teeth.

Boss Fight:
While it is The Trapper's boss fight, the Trader takes over during Phase 2.

Phase 2:
After defeating his first phase, the Trapper flips his mask upside-down, becoming the Trader and revealing they were the same person this whole time.

At the start of this phase, the Trader will play random cards with random extra Sigils in all 8 of her spaces, then after putting all Wolf Pelts played back into your hand and giving you one extra, allowing you to trade. Each Pelt can be used to obtain one of the cards, but any not traded will fight for her.

After the boss fight, just before the Leshy boss fight, if you still have pelts remaining, you can go to the trader event, and it will say that her outpost was abandoned, but "feeling respect for the strange woman" you only take what you can afford.

Act II:
The Trader stands in a storeroom in every main area. She will allow you to buy card packs, Rare cards, and cards from the respective area for Foils.

Rare cards are sold for 4 foils, the top right card is sold for 1 foil, and the other cards are sold for 2 foils.

After showing her a picture of a Pelt in Leshy's Cabin, she flips her head and becomes the Trapper, who initiates battle.

Act III:
The Trader is a disembodied hologram found in the same storeroom in P03's Factory that she could be found in during Act II. This room can be unlocked by traveling to the equivalent location in Botopia and clicking on a lock found there.

When interacting with her in the storage room, she consistently refers to herself in the first person plural (we, us, etc.). It is likely that this has to do with her alternate ego, The Trapper.

You can trade Holo Pelts found in Botopia with her for bits of lore, signified by various Tarot Cards from the Major Arcana, similar to Catarina in The Hex. She will accept 5 Holo Pelts before you exhaust all of their information.

The available cards are The Fool, The Empress, Death, The Devil, and The Tower.

Kaycee's Mod:

Event:
The Trader can be encountered as in Act I, albeit with the possibility of encountering her while having defeated her as early as the second location, due to the randomized order of the three bosses. As in Act I when visiting her just before the final boss, Leshy will say the challenger finds the outpost empty, but 'out of respect for the strange woman', they take only what they can afford.

Battle:
The Trader's role in Kaycee's Mod is roughly the same as in Act I. However, she can be encountered earlier, as the map order is randomized in the mode. If encountered as the first or second boss, in her phase she will fill the board with weaker cards, and only the second row of cards will have sigils.

name: The Trapper
text:
The Trapper is an NPC and boss in Act I and an NPC and opponent in Act II.

He is an odd looking man who traps animals to create and sell Pelts. He and the Trader are the same person, with him seemingly being the lesser, more aggressive personality of the two. Leshy uses the same mask for both, just flips them upside-down.

Act I:

Event:
The Trapper will offer the player Pelts in exchange for teeth. 

The Pelts offered are as follows:
- Rabbit Pelt - Costs 1 to 2 teeth
- Wolf Pelt - Costs 2 to 6 teeth
- Golden Pelt - Costs 3 to 11 teeth

Note: Pelts increase in cost every area, and after beating his boss fight once, his prices will be lowered in every subsequent run.

The player will also receive 1 Rabbit Pelt for free upon encountering the Trapper.

These Pelts may be traded with the Trader for in exchange for cards. See her page for more details.

Boss Fight:
The Trapper is the boss of the Snow Line. He has two phases.

Phase 1:
The Trapper starts with 2 Strange Frogs and 1 Leaping Trap on the board. He will play a variety of cards such as Bullfrogs and Strange Frogs.

If the player hasn't died at least twice, defeating the first phase will result in the Trapper filling the board with Grizzly cards with the Mighty Leap Sigil.

Phase 2:
After defeating his first phase, the Trapper flips his mask upside-down, becoming the Trader and revealing they were the same person this whole time.

At the start of this phase, the Trader will play random cards with random extra Sigils in all 8 of her spaces, then after putting all Wolf Pelts played back into your hand and giving you one extra, allowing you to trade. Each Pelt in your hand, including ones you drew yourself can be used to obtain one of the cards, but any not traded for will fight for her.

Post-Battle:
After they're defeated, the player has their candles relit and proceeds to the Cabin.

After defeating the Trapper for the first time, his prices are permanently reduced in all subsequent runs.

Act II:
The Trapper can be battled by showing the Trader a picture of a Pelt in Leshy's Cabin. After this she will flip her head upside-down and become the Trapper, who will initiate battle.

Battle:
The Trapper will always start by playing a Bullfrog and a Burrowing Trap. After this he will play a random mix of Bullfrogs, Coyotes, and Ravens.

Post-Battle:
After defeating him, he gives the player a Beastly card pack and turns back into the Trader for the rest of the game.

Kaycee's Mod:

Shop:
The Trapper will allow you to purchase the Skinning Knife alongside Pelts.

Battle:
The Trapper's Role in Kaycee's mod is roughly the same as in Act I, however he can be encountered earlier, as the map order is randomized in the mod. If encountered as the first or second boss, he will play weaker cards such as rabbits in the first phase. In the Trader's Phase, she will fill the board with weaker cards, and only the second row of cards will have sigils. 

If the Trapper boss is fought and killed early, both the Trapper and Trader events will be different. Since they are dead, they will no longer appear at their shops but mechanically buying and selling pelts will continue as normal, with Leshy explaining that the player is doing this out of respect for the dead.

name: The Unfinished Boss
text:
The Unfinished Boss is a boss that appears in Act III of Inscryption. It is one of the four Uberbots that the player must defeat in order to enact The Great Transcendence. 

Behavior:
Phase 1:
The Unfinished Boss will begin the fight by asking the player to give them a face. Once the player has decided on the Unfinished Boss's face, it will then ask the player to create a special rule for them to use for the fight. 

The possible presets for the boss's rules are:

Top:
*Everytime your turn starts
*When a card is played
*When a card dies

Bottom:
*A random card takes 5 damage
*One of my cards gains Nano Armor
*I play a L33pB0t
*All cards take 1 damage
*A random card is played
*You lose 1 life

Phase 2:
When the second phase starts, the player will be asked to make a second rule for the boss to use. After a certain amount of turns it is possible for the boss to ask for a third and final rule; however, this is not mandatory.

If rules trigger more than 30 times per turn (infinite loop), P03 will be annoyed and will remove the last added rule.

Related Achievements:

name: Totem
text:
A Totem is an object in Act I of Inscryption that gives an additional Sigil to a specified tribe during combat. 

The player is able to create their own totem when encountering the Woodcarver. Totems are composed of two pieces: the totem head and the totem body. Only one piece of the totem may be acquired per encounter with the Woodcarver, so it will take at least 2 encounters to fully form a totem, unless the player already has the Squirrel head piece. The totem created will apply to all battles until the next Woodcarver encounter, where the player will have the option to modify their totem. Totems cannot be assembled or modified outside of a Woodcarver encounter. 

The Totem Card Battle event provides the enemy with a totem for the duration of the fight. The body of the Totem has a random sigil, and the head of the totem will be of the tribe that primarily appears during the battle.

Amalgam and Hydra are affected by all totems, as they belong to every tribe.

Totem Heads:
This piece defines which tribe is influenced by the totem body. Each tribe has its own totem head piece.

To have access to the Squirrel head, the fourth cabinet puzzle in Leshy's Cabin must be completed. This gives the player the Squirrel head automatically in the current and all future runs. If the player's Squirrels are transformed into Bees by completing the third painting puzzle in the cabin, then the player will have a Squirrel and Insect head in all future runs.

If the Boss Totems challenge is enabled in Kaycee's Mod, each of the boss characters will have their own pre-determined totem head. The Prospector uses the Canine head, The Angler uses Avian, The Trapper/Trader uses Reptile and Leshy uses Insect. The Squirrel totem head cannot be found in this mode.

Totem Bodies:
This piece displays a Sigil which defines the effect applied by the totem on the influenced cards.

Only the Sigils with the meta category Part1Modular are offered to the player, so Sigils such as Repulsive and Omni Strike cannot be obtained. Leshy only has a select number of totem bodies available to him, usually omitting those that do not make sense when not played by the player (e.g. Hoarder or Trinket Bearer).

Sounds (Sounds found by "AManWithAFace"):
Red_noise.wav  plays during a totem battle

Totem_drop.wav  plays once a Totem drops onto the table

Totem_attach.wav  plays when a Totem Head is being screwed onto a Totem Body

Totem_activate.wav  plays once the Player's Totem gives a drawn card a Sigil

Totem disassemble.wav  plays when a Totem Head is being unscrewed off a Totem Body

name: Totem Card Battle
text:
Totem Card Battles are a variation of Card Battles where the enemy is given a Totem bearing a random sigil and the tribe head corresponding to the main tribe played in the battle. Other than that, the battle remains unchanged.

In Kaycee's Mod, the All Totem Battle Challenge causes every regular Card Battle on the map to be replaced with Totem Card Battles.

RED NOISE  plays during a totem battle

name: Uberbots
text:
Uberbots are the bosses in Act III of Inscryption. There are four Uberbots spread across Botopia, each corresponding to a Scrybe found in the corresponding position in the map of Act II.

The Photographer:
They take pictures of the board and can revert it back to that state. You can reset from a hard phase 2 board to an easy to win phase 1 board. Changing to phase 2 does nothing. They are the Uberbot of Foul Backwaters. 

This boss represents Leshy: 
- P03 describes this eerie bot as potentially "waiting in the dark looking for Challengers" much like Leshy.
- Both share an orange color scheme, use a camera and have a "different" way of speaking. 
- Both sit in the dark inside their cabin in the woods, filled with beasts to fight. The name of this Uberbot's area "Foul Backwater" is also based on P03's description of Leshy's "Foul Cabin" 
- Fishbot will remark how it reminds him of "Leshy-Fish."
- It is likely that this bot was made pathetically easy solely due to P03's hatred of Leshy.

The Archivist:
After attacking their bots, they will ask you to pick a file from your computer and put it on the scale. The bigger the file you choose, the more damage it will do. A few file names have special dialogue. If you select a file called Inscryption.exe (doesn't have to be the real game, it's just in the name) they will say "Be careful with that one!" A file named Pony Island.exe will make them say "That poor soul..." and The Hex.exe will make them say "Lionel did what?" These are references to Daniel Mullins' other games. After moving into phase 2, they will tell you to choose a file that is old, and dear to your heart. Then that file will be put into a card. If it is a photo file, The Archivist will replace their face with the photo. Depending on how old the file is, it will give it different stats, although P03 says that if the card dies, the file will be deleted. Even if it does die, P03 adds a file saying that it cannot delete the file due to the file access not giving them the permission to do this, (as then the game could be considered malware) but that you should anyway. If you delete the file afterwards, it will say "You really did it?" and you then get the achievement "Agonizing Remorse". They are the Uberbot of Filthy Corpse World, in the Dank Crypt. 

This boss represents Grimora: 
- They use Gravestones in the start, and the deletion mechanic is similar to how Grimora uses the dead to battle.
- Their location is based on Grimora's crypt from Act II, even including Grimora's well in one location.
- They also use a teal color scheme like Grimora.
- The item required to fight this Uberbot is Grimora's quill.

The Unfinished Boss:
PO3 asks you to create a boss, giving you many options for the gimmick of the fight. This is one of the bosses where its really important to understand your deck before making the gimmick. In Phase 2, you create a second gimmick. Upon drawing Fishbot, he will say "No boss. Make rule. Break game?" Creating a rule that does break the game by going on for too many cycles will cause P03 to get annoyed and disable one of the offending boss gimmicks for the rest of the fight. Additionally, if the fight goes on for a long time, you can create one extra gimmick. They are the Uberbot of Gaudy Gem Land, in the Rickety Old Tower. 

There are some interesting gimmicks you can make. For example: 
- Every time a card dies / A random card takes 5 damage. The board is wiped whenever a card dies, except for nano armored cards or a sufficiently-buffed Ourobot. 
- Every time you play a card / A random card is played. True chaos at its finest. 
- Every time you play a card / I play a L33PBOT. Every single card you play is met with an initial hurdle.
- Every time your turn starts / All cards take 1 damage. Every card is eventually going to die! 

The boss represents Magnificus: 
- P03 likes to pretend he doesn't exist. 
- The ability to choose the gimmicks of the fight aligns with Magnificus' ability to change the sigils of cards. 
- Painting the bosses' face and the paintings used to show the boss rules are based on Magnificus' use of painting.
- The red color scheme for the text is similar to Magnificus' text while talking. 
- Goobert remarks that it reminds him of "The Master".
- They are also located atop a wizard tower like Magnificus was in Act II. 

G0lly:
She starts the battle by playing a Mole. Afterwards, she uses the web to grab people from your friends list to become bots with varying stats, but they are often very powerful. During the boss fight, G0lly tries to give you a card made by other players. If it doesn't work, then she'll give you a Mummy Lord instead. In Phase 2, Golly asks you to return the favor and create a card for someone else. If she can not find one, you receive the card. If she does find somebody, the battle is paused and G0lly comments on how the other player is doing. If the other player wins, Phase 2 is skipped entirely. If not, you receive the card you made and continue Phase 2. The music that G0lly uses is more upbeat to signify innocence. They are the Uberbot of the Resplendent Bastion.

This boss very loosely represents P03, located inside the factory and also having some of P03's physical features such as the head crank and only one arm.

name: Wiseclock
text:
Rulebook: To the user: All creatures on the board will rotate one space clockwise.

The Wiseclock is an item in Kaycee's Mod of Inscryption. When used, all cards rotate one space clockwise.

Unlocking the Wiseclock:
To be able to find and use the Wiseclock, you must complete a painting puzzle in Leshy's Cabin by placing the proper cards on your side of the board. Once done, the Cabin will shake and the Wiseclock can be taken from the painting.
